title: Forward Deployed Engineer (all genders) - Remote Germany or Hungary
description:
About Linro

Linro is a Berlin-based cloud security company building a real-time, agentic cloud-security platform. Teams ship with AI. AI ships with Linro.

Infrastructure changes constantly, and increasingly it's AI agents making the changes. Tools that scan snapshots and flag risk after the fact can't keep up. Linro enforces intended state across the whole lifecycle instead, from commit to runtime: MCP and pre-commit hooks at commit time, blast-radius simulation that blocks bad changes before they ship, and real-time detection, enforcement and auto-remediation in production. Most tools tell you what's wrong. Linro stops it.

We have each been on the receiving end of this problem: Running cloud security at scale, building the platforms underneath it, and shipping in regulated systems where a wrong change isn't an option. Founded in Berlin in 2026 and built fully remote across Europe, Linro has a platform that's real and working, with plenty still to shape.

The role

You would be the engineer who gets Linro running inside a customer's real environment and keeps it running. Our founders and go-to-market team win the customer and own the commercial relationship. You own the technical side: you take a customer from signed agreement to a working install and the first blocked change, and stay on it after go-live for upgrades, incidents and tuning. Part of this happens on-site: you may spend a few days at a customer's office to get an install running or to work through a problem with their team. Everything you learn goes back to engineering and product. This is an engineering role, not a support or sales role, and there is no quota.

What you will do

  • Run customer onboarding end to end: connect the customer's cloud accounts, whichever provider they run on, deploy sensors (managed, or inside the customer's own cluster) and get to a first blocked change fast.

  • Write and tune SQL-based policies and policy packs mapped to each customer's frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIS2, DORA), and keep false positives low.

  • Wire Linro guardrails into the customer's Terraform and CI/CD workflows and into their AI coding agents through MCP.

  • Run Linro in production at the customer: monitor, upgrade and respond when it breaks. Debug inside their environment, hand reproducible findings to engineering, and fix what you can yourself.

  • Close the loop: structured feedback to product and engineering, reusable playbooks for the next customer, and a seat in scoping calls so that what we promise is what installs.


What we are looking for

  • 5 to 6+ years of customer-facing technical delivery (forward deployed or solutions engineering, SRE or platform consulting), deploying infrastructure or security software in customer environments and keeping it running afterwards.

  • Hands-on cloud experience: you have run real workloads, identity and access, networking and audit logging on at least one major cloud, and you pick up the others quickly.

  • You are a solid engineer. You write real code in Go or Python for integrations and tooling, read Go services, and are comfortable with SQL and APIs.

  • You use AI coding agents daily, such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, and have hands-on MCP experience.

  • You understand how companies work: change management, approvals, release and audit processes, and how to fit Linro into them.

  • Restricted-network experience: proxies, private networking, data residency, self-hosted or in-cluster installs.

  • Communication and comfort with ambiguity. You explain trade-offs clearly to engineers and executives, set honest expectations, and keep making progress when requirements are still unclear. Fluent English.

  • Open to travel. To customers across Europe and the US, up to roughly a quarter of your time.

Nice to have

  • Turning compliance frameworks (e.g. SOC 2, ISO 27001) into concrete controls.

  • Policy-as-code (OPA/Rego, Sentinel, Cedar) or CSPM tooling.

How we work

We work remotely across Europe. We get the whole team together in person somewhere in Europe once a quarter for a few days. We work async by default, write things down, and protect people's focus time.

What we offer

  • Real ownership. You own every customer deployment from day one, with direct access to the founders and to the engineers who built what you are deploying.

  • Meaningful equity. You are an early employee, and your stake reflects it.

  • Competitive salary, benchmarked to the market.

  • A quarterly European offsite, and a team that takes both the mission and each other's time seriously.

The honest version

This is early. You will often be the first person to run Linro in a customer's environment, and you will write the playbooks as you go. If you want a polished onboarding process and a stable product surface, this is not it. If you want to sit between a new category and the customers who need it, and you like the idea of deploying the thing that keeps AI agents from breaking production, we should talk.

Linro is a Berlin-based cloud security company building a real-time, agentic cloud-security platform. Teams ship with AI. AI ships with Linro.

Infrastructure changes constantly, and increasingly it's AI agents making the changes. Tools that scan snapshots and flag risk after the fact can't keep up. Linro enforces intended state across the whole lifecycle instead, from commit to runtime: MCP and pre-commit hooks at commit time, blast-radius simulation that blocks bad changes before they ship, and real-time detection, enforcement and auto-remediation in production. Most tools tell you what's wrong. Linro stops it.

We have each been on the receiving end of this problem: Running cloud security at scale, building the platforms underneath it, and shipping in regulated systems where a wrong change isn't an option. Founded in Berlin in 2026 and built fully remote across Europe, Linro has a platform that's real and working, with plenty still to shape.

The role

You would be one of our first infrastructure hires, taking day-to-day operation of the platform off the CTO. Linro enforces policy on other people's cloud infrastructure, so our own has to be reliable, reproducible and auditable. You own production: how Linro runs for each customer, how it upgrades, and how we know it is unhealthy before a customer does.

What you will do

  • Own production reliability: SLOs, alerting, on-call and blameless postmortems for the control plane and every customer installation.

  • Make the install fleet boring: provisioning, maintenance windows and safe auto-upgrades across SaaS and self-hosted installs.

  • Fix the open reliability work: sensor memory ceilings and OOM visibility, ClickHouse cost and capacity, and the health of Postgres, PGMQ and Temporal.

  • Evolve the platform: Terraform and Terragrunt, Helm, GitHub Actions with short-lived OIDC credentials, local development (Tilt, Coder), and staging and production environments, with guardrails for humans and AI agents alike.

  • Produce audit-ready operations: backups, disaster recovery and continuity tests with evidence for SOC 2 and ISO 27001.

What we are looking for

  • Hands-on operation of AWS, GCP or Azure in production, AWS preferred. Not just deploying to it, actually running it: accounts and access management, networking and the failure modes. We run across several clouds, so you pick up the others quickly.

  • 3+ years running production Kubernetes with Helm, including debugging OOMs, resource limits and failed rollouts.

  • Terraform in multi-environment setups, with CI/CD in GitHub Actions and short-lived credentials.

  • Go, or Python and a wish to learn Go. You read and write code in the services you operate.

  • Observability and SLOs: symptom-based alerting with Prometheus, Grafana or OpenTelemetry, and the discipline to delete noisy alerts.

  • Production Postgres: backups, point-in-time recovery, migrations and upgrades.

  • Incident ownership: on-call, leading incidents and writing postmortems that change something.

  • Security-minded operations: least privilege, secrets handling, access reviews and audit trails.

  • You work with AI agents every day, including for infrastructure changes, and know where to trust them and where to check their output.

Nice to have

  • Operating Temporal, queues or ClickHouse, including cost tuning.

  • Shipping and upgrading software in customer-run or self-hosted environments.

  • Compliance operations: SOC 2, ISO 27001 or PCI DSS evidence.

  • Using AI coding agents safely for infrastructure work.

  • Early-stage startup experience, or having been a founding infrastructure engineer.

How we work

We work remotely across Europe. On-call is part of this role. We will be open about how the rotation works and compensate it. We get the whole team together in person somewhere in Europe once a quarter for a few days. We work async by default, write things down, and protect people's focus time.

What we offer

  • Real ownership. You own production and the platform underneath it, with direct contact with the engineers and a say in how we build.

  • Meaningful equity. You are an early employee, and your stake reflects it.

  • Competitive salary, benchmarked to the market.

  • A quarterly European offsite, and a team that takes both the mission and each other's time seriously.

The honest version

This is early. Our infrastructure is defined as code, but parts of it are still being moved into CI, runbooks are thin, and some environments are rougher than others. You would inherit something that works, not something polished. If you want a mature platform team with a clear roadmap for the next two years, this is not it. If you want to build the operational backbone of a security product from close to the start, and you like the idea of running the thing that keeps AI agents from breaking production, we should talk.

title: Senior Quantum Fault-Tolerance Architect (f/m/d)

eleQtron develops and operates full-stack quantum computers based on trapped-ion technology. Our approach combines laser schemes for cooling/initialization/readout, engineered magnetic-field gradient induced coupling (MAGIC) combined with microwave control for universal gate sets, and advanced quantum control techniques and dedicated firmware to work within the high-fidelity regime and below the error threshold of quantum error correction (QEC).


A central objective of our technology roadmap is the realization of fault-tolerant quantum computing. To achieve this goal, we combine the above high-fidelity quantum hardware with microscopic physics-based modelling, hardware–software co-design, advanced characterization and benchmarking techniques, and detailed numerical simulations to model system performance realistically and identify the optimal QEC strategy and the associated system requirements.

As part of our initiative towards fault-tolerant quantum computing, we are expanding our Foundations & Concepts team and are looking for a Senior Quantum Fault-Tolerance Architect (f/m/d) to help establish and grow this strategic activity within the company.

title: Senior Fullstack Entwickler PHP/Laravel (m/w/d) - Remote, 4-Tage-Woche
description:
Intro

Du möchtest an einer Legal-Tech-Anwendung arbeiten, die für E-Commerce-Unternehmen wie eine digitale Rechtsabteilung funktioniert? Du denkst Systeme vom Datenmodell bis zur Oberfläche, konzipierst gern technische Lösungen und übernimmst Verantwortung dafür, dass sie am Ende auch so umgesetzt werden? Dann bist du als Senior Fullstack-Entwickler (m/w/d) / Senior Webentwickler PHP/Laravel (m/w/d) beim Händlerbund genau richtig!

Bei uns entwickelst du an einer Plattform, die rechtliche Prozesse digital abbildet und automatisiert. Von der Erstellung rechtlicher Inhalte über Vertrags- und Prüfprozesse bis hin zu Datenschutz- und Sicherheitsfragen. Dazu gehören Schnittstellen und Plugins, über die unsere Inhalte in die Shopsysteme unserer Mitglieder gelangen, sowie Integrationen mit Partnersystemen. Ziel ist es, komplexe rechtliche Anforderungen in verlässliche, verständliche und effiziente digitale Workflows zu überführen.

In dieser Rolle übernimmst du die technische Leitung von Projekten, die wir in kleinen Projektteams umsetzen: Du konzipierst Lösungen, verantwortest die Umsetzung, leitest andere Entwickler im Projekt an und hältst alle Beteiligten über den Stand auf dem Laufenden. Kleinere Projekte setzt du eigenständig komplett um, bei größeren arbeitest du im Team mit Laravel und Livewire im Stack.


Deine Aufgaben

  • Technische Konzeption: Analyse von Anforderungen, Entwurf der Lösungsarchitektur, Festlegung von Datenmodellen und Schnittstellen sowie Einschätzung von Aufwänden für Features und Projekte.

  • Ownership für die Umsetzung: Verantwortung dafür, dass ein Projekt von der Konzeption bis zum Go-live ankommt. Aufgaben schneiden und priorisieren, Fortschritt im Blick behalten, technische Entscheidungen treffen und Blocker aus dem Weg räumen.

  • Anleitung & Wissenstransfer: Fachliche Führung weiterer Entwickler im Projekt durch klare technische Vorgaben, Pairing und Code Reviews im Backend wie im Frontend. Wissen über Architektur und Entscheidungen landet im Team und in der Dokumentation, nicht nur bei dir.

  • Reporting: Regelmäßige, verständliche Berichte zu Stand, Risiken und nächsten Schritten an Team Lead, Product Owner und Stakeholder.

  • Fullstack-Entwicklung: Umsetzung mit Laravel, Livewire, Alpine.js, Flux UI und Tailwind CSS. Kleinere Projekte eigenständig von Anfang bis Ende, größere im Projektteam.

  • Partneranbindungen & Integrationen: Lösungsevaluierung, Umsetzung und Dokumentation von Schnittstellen zu Partner- und Drittsystemen.

  • Architektur & Technologie-Evaluation: Mitgestaltung von Architektur, Entwicklungsstandards und Tooling; Evaluation neuer Technologien, Frameworks und KI-Einsatzmöglichkeiten im Hinblick auf ihren konkreten Nutzen für Produkt und Team.


Dein Profil

Technisch

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung mit PHP & Laravel: Entwicklung von Webanwendungen über den gesamten Stack, im Frontend idealerweise mit Livewire, Alpine.js, Flux UI und Tailwind CSS.

  • Konzeption & technische Leitung: Erfahrung darin, technische Konzepte zu erarbeiten und deren Umsetzung zu verantworten, allein oder als technische Leitung eines Projektteams.

  • Code Reviews über den gesamten Stack: Praxis im Review von Backend- und Frontend-Code und die Fähigkeit, Feedback so zu geben, dass andere daran wachsen.

  • Testerfahrung: Sicherer Umgang mit PHPUnit oder Pest und Erfahrung mit Teststrategien in größeren Codebasen. Tests sind für dich Teil der Umsetzung, nicht Nacharbeit.

  • Datenbanken & APIs: Sicherer Umgang mit relationalen Datenbanken, Datenmodellierung und API-Design.

  • Agile Teamarbeit: Erfahrung in agilen Teams, idealerweise mit Scrum, inklusive enger Zusammenarbeit und kontinuierlichem Austausch.


Nice to Have, aber kein Muss

  • DevOps-Erfahrung: Cloud-Systeme, PaaS-Plattformen, Container, CI/CD oder Linux-Serveradministration (z.B. DigitalOcean und Laravel Cloud)

  • Erfahrung mit Shopsystemen und der Entwicklung von Plugins oder Apps dafür (z.B. Shopify oder JTL)

  • Gespür für UX und Erfahrung in der Gestaltung benutzerfreundlicher Oberflächen

  • Erfahrung mit Event-basierten Architekturen, Queues oder asynchronen Verarbeitungsprozessen

  • Erfahrung mit der Integration von LLM-APIs in Produktfeatures (Prompting, Evaluierung, Guardrails)


Persönlich

  • Ownership: Du fühlst dich für das Ergebnis eines Projekts verantwortlich. Von der ersten Skizze bis zum Go-live und darüber hinaus und nicht nur für deine eigenen Tickets.

  • Systemisches Denken: Du siehst die Auswirkungen von Änderungen über Komponenten- und Teamgrenzen hinweg.

  • Strukturierte Kommunikation: Du bereitest den Stand eines Projekts für technische und nicht-technische Beteiligte verständlich auf, auch dann, wenn etwas nicht nach Plan läuft.

  • Pragmatismus: Du findest die Balance zwischen sauberer Lösung und pragmatischem Fortschritt.

  • Wissenstransfer: Du hast Freude daran, Wissen weiterzugeben und andere im Team besser zu machen, bspw. in Reviews, Pairings und Dokumentation.

  • KI als Werkzeug: Du nutzt KI-Tools im Entwicklungsalltag selbstverständlich und beurteilst nüchtern, wo sie im Produkt echten Nutzen bringen und wo nicht.


Warum wir?

Code. Chill. Repeat.

  • 4 Tage Code – 3 Tage du selbst: Bei uns ist die 4-Tage-Woche Standard. Kein Gimmick, sondern Realität. Du arbeitest remote oder im Leipziger Büro – so, wie du am besten performst. Flexzeiten, kein Micromanagement, volle Eigenverantwortung. Und ja: unbefristet von Anfang an.

  • Dein Stack, dein Style: Wir stehen auf smarte Lösungen, sauberen Code und Menschen, die mitdenken. Du willst mitentscheiden, ausprobieren und nicht nur Tickets abarbeiten? Here you go. Plus: Mentoring, Weiterbildung nach Bedarf und Raum für echte Weiterentwicklung.

  • Remote first, Team always: Trotz Remote bleibt das Teamgefühl. Wir feiern Releases, grillen im Sommer und stoßen auf tolle Ideen an. Dein Bürohund ist bei uns genauso willkommen wie dein Lieblingseditor.

  • Professionalität: echte Qualität statt Show-off. Wir leben agile Entwicklung mit klaren Iterationen und direktem Feedback. Du arbeitest mit modernen, professionellen Tools, mit klaren Rollen und Verantwortlichkeiten – du weißt genau, was dein Job ist und hast die Freiheit, ihn so zu machen, wie es richtig ist. Sauberer Code, smarte Entscheidungen und ein Team, das zusammenarbeitet. Professionalität heißt hier: Du kannst dich auf das konzentrieren, was du am besten kannst – entwickeln.

  • Snacks, Swag & Softdrinks: Obst, Müsli, Kaffee, Wasser – alles for free. Kein Dresscode. Komm, wie du bist. Hauptsache du fühlst dich wohl.

  • Perks, die was bringen: Kita-Zuschuss, Unterstützung bei der Altersvorsorge, Leipziger Jobticket oder sportliche Angebote für deinen Ausgleich – vom Homegym bis zum Fitnessstudio für Kopf und Körper.


Dein Weg zu uns

Keine Lust auf lange Anschreiben? Kein Problem! Erzähl uns einfach kurz, warum du Teil vom Händlerbund werden möchtest und warum wir gut zu dir passen. Nutze dazu die Möglichkeit dich online über unser Bewerbungsformular zu bewerben.

title: Co-Founder & CTO @ AI Model Efficiency Engine Venture, Berlin
description:
This is an Atlantic portfolio venture.

About the Venture

AI models have moved faster than most companies’ ability to put them to work. The capabilities are there; knowing how to combine them effectively is still catching up.

Frontier labs naturally put their own models first. Companies often follow suit, asking one general-purpose model to handle ten very different jobs. We believe there is far more to unlock in the models that already exist, even before the next generation arrives. That is the opportunity we are building around.

We bring closed providers and open-weight models together behind a single API. With no proprietary model to promote, we can choose the right combination for the task. Our engine breaks requests into their component parts, routes each to the right model within a cost budget, fine-tunes on customer data and checks the result against agreed quality standards. Think ten specialists working on ten pieces, rather than one generalist carrying the whole task.

Lower costs matter because of what they make possible: giving a small team the freedom to build something that would previously have required a much larger one.

Our founder was selected for Slush 20 Under 20, awarded by Anthropic, Slush, Index Ventures and Sifted, and brings considerable drive, a hands-on approach and a strong sense of urgency to building the company. We closed our pre-seed round in two weeks. With people already waiting to use the product, we are looking for a technical co-founder to help shape what comes next and bring it into production.

About the Role

As co-founder and CTO, you will help shape the company as well as its technology. Working alongside the founder as an eye-level partner, you will turn the ambition into an architecture, a product and an engineering team capable of delivering it.a

Your remit spans the efficiency engine, the platform beneath it and the people building both. You will lead our founding AI engineer and backend platform engineer, grow the team and establish the standards that guide its work. You have led engineering before, but stayed close to the code, and want to keep building as your responsibilities grow.

Two things define the technical challenge here. Efficiency is the product itself, so routing, fine-tuning, caching, quantization and open-weight serving sit at the heart of the roadmap. Agentic engineering is also central to how we work. You will set the standard for using individual agents and entire agent fleets effectively, building the harnesses and workflows that allow a small team to move quickly while retaining sound engineering judgement.

There is a lot to build and an ambitious timeline ahead. We work with relentless intensity, move quickly from decisions to execution and look for people who take initiative and see things through. You will have the scope to make consequential decisions early, and the responsibility to turn them into something that works.

What you’ll do

You will move between architecture, code and company building, setting the technical direction while building the team that delivers it.

  • Lead the engineering team: guide our founding AI engineer and backend platform engineer, review their work and establish the engineering and operational standards, including on-call and incident response.

  • Build the team: lead technical hiring and decide how engineering grows as the company develops.

  • Set the technical direction: make the architectural calls, shape the roadmap and decide what we build ourselves and where we use existing tools and services.

  • Develop the efficiency engine: bring together routing, semantic and prefix caching, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, distillation, quantization and batching, with inference economics informing each decision.

  • Own open-weight serving: choose and operate vLLM, SGLang or equivalent, including GPU capacity and European hosting, alongside closed providers through a single interface.

  • Make quality measurable: build rigorous eval harnesses and the evidence needed to establish whether a cheaper route still meets the agreed standard.

  • Build the platform underneath it: own the gateway API, provider layer, identity and tenancy, precise usage and cost accounting, secure storage of customer keys and European infrastructure as code, with GDPR and data residency requirements built in.

  • Stay hands-on: write code and play an active part in designing and building the platform and cost-efficiency systems. Develop our agentic engineering setup, from harness design and benchmarking to the agent workflows that help the team ship.

  • Represent the company technically: bring depth and clarity to customer pilots, enterprise security reviews and investor conversations.

About You

You have grown into engineering leadership without losing the instinct to build. When faced with a difficult problem, you explore what would make it possible and look for a workable path through it, weighing failure modes alongside unit economics. AI has changed how you work, and you have taken the time to understand where it helps, where it fails and how to use it well.

We are looking for depth in five areas:

  • Engineering leadership: you have been a CTO, VP Engineering, Head of Engineering or engineering lead, ideally in a startup. You have hired and led engineers, established standards and taken responsibility for both the architecture and what the team shipped.

  • Backend and platform engineering: you bring deep experience in distributed systems, API design, streaming, Postgres, Kubernetes, Terraform and cloud operations, with a broad understanding of what makes a platform reliable and scalable. You have taken systems into production, operated them under significant load and worked through incidents yourself.

  • LLM cost efficiency: you have reduced costs in a production system and can explain the numbers, the decisions behind them and the trade-offs involved. Your experience covers techniques such as LoRA or QLoRA, routing, caching, quantization, distillation and batching, grounded in an understanding of serving economics.

  • Open-weight models in production: you have served, tuned, evaluated and operated open models under load, including the GPU and capacity decisions that come with them.

  • Agentic engineering: you build on strong coding fundamentals, with practical experience running agent fleets and designing and benchmarking their harnesses. You can reason independently about the code they produce and take responsibility for its quality.

You also bring a disciplined approach to LLM benchmarking: thoughtful eval design, statistical honesty and a willingness to reproduce results before relying on them.

Fluent English is required; German is a plus.

Nice to have

  • A strong open-source record, particularly in AI infrastructure or inference, with real users.

  • Experience with LiteLLM, NVIDIA NIM, TGI, llama.cpp or similar, and with self-hosted or air-gapped enterprise deployments.

  • Experience with European cloud providers such as Scaleway, Hetzner or OVH.

  • Experience working in startups tackling similar technical challenges.

Why Join

With the pre-seed round closed and the first steps already taken, you will join at a point where there is momentum to build on and considerable room to shape what comes next. You will build alongside the founder, choose and grow the engineering team, and receive co-founder equity in the business you help create.

The architecture, efficiency engine, security model and engineering culture are all still yours to shape. The decisions you make now will become the foundations for everything that follows.

We are entering a market where competitors have larger teams, more funding and an earlier start. Our conviction is that technical depth, focused decisions and a small team that works well together give us a meaningful opportunity to compete. For the right person, that is an interesting challenge to take on, with substantial ownership over how we approach it.

This is a full-time commitment, based in our Berlin office five days a week, starting as soon as possible.

About Us

Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact.

We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem.

Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work.

At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team.

Visit www.perk.com to learn more.

What you'll do:

You'll own building the experiences of our group travel and events product, an all-in-one platform helping companies book providers and coordinate their attendees. This is a complex, multi-sided offering spanning corporate event planners, event support specialists on the Perk side, suppliers and event participants. You'll be the design lead shaping how those experiences come together in the product and within the broader Perk platform (travel, spend).

At Perk, we believe that real-life connections have greater value than ever. While the world has embraced hybrid work, the need for teams to gather, brainstorm, and celebrate in person has skyrocketed. That’s why we built Perk Events.

Born from our internal innovation incubator, Perk Events is our newest vertical. We are moving from "start-up" to "scale-up," and we are looking for a Senior Front End Engineer. This isn't just an ordinary Engineering role; it’s an opportunity to disrupt a legacy industry with AI-driven tech, and lead a world-class team driving towards ambitious revenue goals.

You'll own building the experiences of our group travel and events product, an all-in-one platform helping companies book providers and coordinate their attendees. This is a complex, multi-sided offering spanning corporate event planners, event support specialists on the Perk side, suppliers and event participants. You'll be the design lead shaping how those experiences come together in the product and within the broader Perk platform (travel, spend).

Some examples of what it means to be a Senior at Perk

  • Shape the bigger picture. You won't just build features, you'll refine the what to build and why. At Perk, senior engineers are expected to go beyond the technical solution and focus on the problem itself. You'll contribute to your squad's quarterly goals and long-term vision alongside your Product Manager and Engineering Manager.

  • Architect for today and tomorrow. When a big change is needed in how our platform works, you'll be the one writing the design documents that lay the foundation. You'll become a guardian of your team's technical quality; spotting areas of investment, proactively managing technical debt, and making sure we don't let "busy work" crowd out the work that truly matters. At Perk, we believe in impact over effort: our customers see results, not the hours behind them. Your job is to make sure we're always investing our energy where it counts most.

  • Lead across boundaries. Your influence won't stop at your own squad. You'll communicate complex ideas across multiple teams, proactively identify who needs to be involved, and drive alignment across the broader organisation. Whether it's coordinating a cross-squad initiative, contributing to one of our engineering guilds (where engineers from different teams align on shared technical topics), or pairing with architects on solution discovery, you'll operate comfortably beyond your immediate team.

  • Raise the bar for everyone around you. Senior engineers at Perk are mentors, coaches, and bar raisers. You'll support less experienced colleagues through direct mentorship, thoughtful feedback during reviews, and by modelling what great engineering looks like in practice. You'll help Engineering Managers understand where the team needs to grow technically, and you'll use spaces like guild meetings, design doc reviews, and pairing sessions to lift the overall standard. At Perk, we are a team, the team's success is your success.

AI at Perk
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

How We Work

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume.

Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams

All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @perk.com or @externalperk.com, our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com, and we will confirm whether it is legitimate.

  • Un moteur de jeu puissant et innovant : adaptation dynamique de l'offre de jeu, parties de poker hautement configurables, détection de fraude
  • Une architecture distribuée et scalable conçue pour traiter en temps réel les flux de la plateforme

Contexte
L'offre de paris sportifs chez Winamax repose sur le traitement en temps réel de flux massifs de données et l'ajustement continu de probabilités. Pour garantir la cohérence entre les cotes et l'exposition financière de Winamax, l'analyse automatisée des mouvements de marché, du volume des mises et des activités atypiques est devenue un enjeu stratégique.
 
La question à laquelle doit répondre le stage : 
Comment détecter algorithmiquement les incohérences de probabilités et les volumes atypiques en temps réel pour fournir un Indice de Confiance fiable, capable d'assister la prise de décision ?

Objectifs du stage
  • Modéliser la cohérence des cotes et un Indice de Confiance : Concevoir des modèles statistiques pour repérer les décalages de probabilités et évaluer en temps réel la fiabilité des activités à fort volume, en croisant la notoriété de l'événement et son historique
  • Intégrer le module au cœur de l'outil trading existant : Développer une brique algorithmique performante qui s'interface directement avec l'application métier des traders, afin d'enrichir leurs outils
  • Validation & mesure de performance (Backtesting) : Tester et calibrer les modèles sur des historiques massifs de données pour maximiser leur précision, minimiser les fausses alertes et mesurer l'impact réel de l'outil sur l'activité

    • Les points d'attention
  • Temps réel et faible latence : capacité à traiter des flux à haute fréquence (milliers d'actualisations et d'activités par seconde) sans ralentir la réactivité des outils
  • Volume de données et backtesting : manipulation de séries temporelles complexes et capacité à tester/ajuster les modèles sur des bases historiques de plusieurs millions de lignes
  • Précision du ciblage (taux de faux positifs) : nécessité d'ajuster finement les seuils statistiques pour remonter des signaux réellement pertinents sans engorger l'outil d'alertes inutiles

The role

As our Senior Data Engineer, you'll own AQEMIA's data platform end to end — from ingestion through the pipeline to the trusted, model-ready datasets that power science, ML and analytics. What makes this role distinctive is the data itself: chemical structures, molecular conformations, physics- and ML-based predictions, and experimental results from CROs and partners.

A core part of the work is modelling these scientific entities well — establishing canonical identity, provenance and trustworthy lineage across heterogeneous, often messy sources — so scientists, and increasingly AI agents, can rely on them. You'll work at the intersection of software engineering, data infrastructure and scientific research, with real scope to shape architecture rather than just execute against it.

  • Production experience with a cloud warehouse (we use Snowflake) and a transformation framework (we use dbt).

  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform) and modern data warehousing (e.g. Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift) and object storage.
  • Experience in drug discovery, biotech, pharma or deeptech environments.
  • Exposure to AI-driven or data-intensive workflows, or experience working across disciplines (e.g. biology ↔ ML ↔ chemistry).

title: Business Unit Director Own to Operate
description:
Wil jij eindverantwoordelijk zijn voor de performance en verdere opschaling van een internationaal portfolio van energie-assets? En krijg je energie van het combineren van strategie, operations, finance, technologie en people leadership? Voor onze Own to Operate (OtO) business unit zoeken wij een Business Unit Director die de organisatie en het portfolio naar een volgende fase van professionalisering, performance en schaalbare groei brengt.

Vandaag bestaat het operationele portfolio uit 8 assets. Met 4 assets in aanbouw en een duidelijke groeistrategie bouwen we dit uit naar circa 25 operationele assets in 2032. Jij speelt een sleutelrol in die transitie: van een nationaal portfolio naar een internationaal, datagedreven en gestandaardiseerd operating model waarin assets en teams over landen heen optimaal samenwerken en presteren.

Jouw rol

Als Business Unit Director OtO ben je eindverantwoordelijk voor een internationaal portfolio van operationele assets én voor de organisatie die dit portfolio naar de volgende fase van professionalisering en schaalbare groei brengt. Je bepaalt de strategische koers, investeringsprioriteiten en operationele standaarden, en geeft direct leiding aan de Asset Managers/Regiomanagers en de managers van de centrale teams (nu 35-40 fte, groeiend naar 100 fte). Je stimuleert samenwerking over landen en assets heen en bouwt aan een cultuur waarin veiligheid, eigenaarschap en performance centraal staan, binnen een business unit met activiteiten in Noordwest-Europa, de Baltics en Oost-Europa.

Wat ga je doen?

  • Je bent eindverantwoordelijk voor de portfolio-P&L en bewaakt de financiële performance van energie, certificaten, biogene CO₂, biomassa, OPEX en CAPEX. Je begeleidt de groei van 8 operationele units, via de 4 assets die momenteel in aanbouw zijn, naar circa 25 assets in 2032.

  • Je geeft direct leiding aan Asset Managers/Regiomanagers en de managers van de centrale teams. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor een sterke bezetting, ontwikkeling van leiderschap en een veilige werkomgeving.

  • Je stelt de operationele en financiële kaders, governance-structuren en mandaten binnen de business unit vast en bouwt deze verder uit met het oog op de internationale groei.

  • Je bouwt het portfolio uit tot een datagedreven operatie: één asset-managementomgeving over alle landen, uniforme instrumentatie en datakwaliteit per plant en cross-plant benchmarking op basis van actuele meetdata in plaats van rapportages achteraf.

  • Je stuurt actief op de performance van het portfolio en maakt onder andere beschikbaarheid, methaanyield versus theoretische yield, ongeplande stilstand en CI-score tot concrete stuurvariabelen voor de organisatie. We nemen het first-reference risico op onze eigen assets voordat we oplossingen aan klanten aanbieden.

  • Je vertaalt groepsbrede programma's, zoals ERP, PDM en One Way of Working, naar de dagelijkse praktijk binnen de business unit en zorgt dat deze daadwerkelijk bijdragen aan performance en schaalbaarheid.

  • Je hebt een formele rol in het investeringsproces van nieuwe ontwikkelprojecten door mede-akkoord te geven vóór FID. Vanuit jouw operationele expertise voed je de business case, het ontwerp en de operationele uitgangspunten van nieuwe assets.

  • Vanaf FID ben je vanuit de business unit eigenaar van een succesvolle voorbereiding op de operatie en de overdracht van EPC naar operatie. Je borgt dat KPI's, data, documentatie, onderhoudsconcepten, operationele standaarden en performance vanaf dag één goed zijn georganiseerd.

  • Je vertegenwoordigt de business unit richting de Executive Board en onderhoudt relaties met relevante interne en externe stakeholders.


Wie ben jij?

Je bent een ervaren leider die gewend is om verantwoordelijkheid te nemen voor complexe, kapitaalintensieve assets en internationale teams. Je combineert strategisch overzicht met voldoende operationele scherpte om te weten waar performance in de praktijk wordt gemaakt. Je hebt bovendien bewezen dat je een organisatie kunt opschalen, standaardiseren en professionaliseren zonder ondernemerschap en eigenaarschap te verliezen.

Je brengt mee:

  • WO werk- en denkniveau.

  • Minimaal 10 jaar relevante ervaring in asset management, exploitatie of een vergelijkbare eindverantwoordelijke rol binnen een kapitaalintensieve en vergunninggevoelige sector.

  • Aantoonbare P&L-verantwoordelijkheid op portfolioniveau.

  • Ervaring met het opschalen en standaardiseren van een internationale operatie, inclusief het integreren van nieuwe of overgenomen assets in één werkwijze, inclusief het aansturen van internationale managementteams en het bouwen van een professionele organisatiestructuur.

  • Sterke inhoudelijke kennis van technologie en exploitatie, bij voorkeur binnen biogas, biomethaan, biomassa of een vergelijkbare energie- of procesomgeving.

  • Aantoonbare ervaring met het digitaliseren van een operationele omgeving: bijvoorbeeld monitoring, conditiebewaking, predictive maintenance of datagedreven procesoptimalisatie. Belangrijk is dat je dit niet als IT-project benadert, maar kunt aantonen dat data en digitalisering daadwerkelijk resultaat hebben opgeleverd in de operatie en P&L.

  • ervaring met offtake- en certificaatstructuren, waaronder GoO en CI-score, en met prijsrisico en hedging op portfolioniveau.

  • Het vermogen om op boardniveau te opereren en complexe onderwerpen helder, overtuigend en besluitgericht te presenteren.

  • Sterke stakeholdermanagementvaardigheden, zowel intern als extern.

  • Uitstekende beheersing van Nederlands en Engels. Duits is een pré.

Ons aanbod

  • Goede arbeidsvoorwaarden en een salaris passend bij werkervaring en opleiding;

  • Jaarlijkse aantrekkelijke winstdeling (uitgekeerd in september) bij een dienstverband van minimaal 12 maanden;

  • Uitstekende pensioenregeling;

  • Reiskostenvergoeding woon-werkverkeer van €0,23 per km;

  • Werken in een internationaal familiebedrijf waar jouw ideeën ertoe doen en successen samen worden gevierd;

  • Aansluiten in een team met zowel startende als ervaren professionals;

  • Vanaf oktober 2026 werken in een volledig nieuw, duurzaam gebouwd kantoorgebouw voorzien van de modernste duurzame faciliteiten in Hengelo.

Over HoSt Group

HoSt Group is een internationale technologieleider op het gebied van duurzame energieoplossingen. Vanuit onze vestigingen ontwikkelen, bouwen en onderhouden wij innovatieve installaties voor hernieuwbare gassen, duurzame warmte, groene waterstof en CO₂-afvang. Als familiebedrijf combineren wij ondernemerschap, innovatie en een sterke focus op duurzaamheid.

title: Senior Product Developer
description:
Take the lead on innovative CO₂ technologies: from idea to global impact!

Are you an experienced technical professional who takes complex technologies to the next level? Do you want to take overall responsibility for the development and standardisation of innovative carbon capture solutions that are implemented worldwide? If so, we can offer you a key role within one of the fastest-growing technologies of the energy transition.

About HoSt Group & Bright Renewables

HoSt Group is a global leader in the development and implementation of high-tech systems for the production of renewable energy from waste streams. With projects in more than 45 countries and offices in the Netherlands, France, Poland, Latvia and the US, amongst others, we contribute every day to the energy transition and a cleaner world.

As a family-run business, founded in 1991, we combine innovation with a down-to-earth approach. We give our people the space to grow, show initiative and contribute to a sustainable future.

Bright Renewables is a supplier of technologies for renewable gas and CO₂ capture, offering global solutions from production to maintenance. As part of the HoSt Group, we work with over 600 colleagues worldwide, 300 of whom are based at our head office in Enschede.

The role

As a Senior Product Developer at Bright Renewables, you will be part of a multidisciplinary business unit comprising more than 80 professionals. Based at our office in Enschede, you will work in a small team of four within Product Management and report to the Product Management Manager. In this role, you will be the driving force behind the further development and standardisation of our sustainable technologies.

You will draw up product development plans, monitor the associated budgets and act as the first point of contact for product standards in relation to Engineering, Sales, Site Support and our suppliers. In doing so, you will work closely with colleagues from Project Management, Engineering, Software and Sales.

Your responsibilities

As a Senior Product Developer, you will have overall responsibility for the further development of our Carbon Capture technology. You will help shape the product strategy, translate market developments into technical innovations and steer the product development roadmap. In doing so, you will have a significant say in investment decisions, standardisation issues and technological decision-making.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Drawing up the annual product development plan and monitoring the associated budget;

  • Taking ownership of the technical standards and long-term development of our Carbon Capture technology;

  • Initiating and implementing product improvements, new functionalities and technical standards that contribute to the further professionalisation and scalability of our Carbon Capture technology;

  • Carrying out technical analyses and identifying opportunities for improvement to continuously optimise the performance, reliability, cost-efficiency and standardisation of our systems;

  • Managing product development and maintenance activities, monitoring progress, setting priorities and ensuring timely decision-making and delivery;

  • ·Acting as a technical sparring partner for Sales on commercial and strategic customer issues.

  • Building and maintaining strategic partnerships with international suppliers and technology partners.


What are we looking for?

  • A completed technical degree at Master’s level (e.g. Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering or similar);

  • At least 5 to 8 years’ practical experience in a technical product development environment, or a background in engineering;

  • Experience of independently managing complex development projects and making technical decisions at product level;

  • Experience of stakeholder management within multidisciplinary and international organisations is an advantage.

  • A proactive and committed approach to work, with a pragmatic mindset;

  • A results-oriented approach and the drive to achieve success together with the team;

  • A good command of both Dutch and English.

What makes this role attractive?

In this role, you will have the opportunity to shape the direction of an international applied technology platform. You will have a direct influence on the technical direction of our Carbon Capture solutions and will work alongside experienced specialists on the next generation of sustainable energy systems.

Our offer

  • Good terms of employment and a salary commensurate with your work experience and qualifications;

  • An attractive annual profit-sharing scheme (paid in September) after a minimum of 12 months’ service;

  • An excellent pension scheme;

  • Travel allowance for commuting: €0.23 per km in accordance with the terms and conditions of employment;

  • An annual holiday allowance of 8%;

  • The option to work 32 or 40 hours per week;

title: Research Staff, Voice AI Foundations - Remote
description:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity

Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone.


The Role

As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems:

  • Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio.

  • Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech.

  • Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”.

  • Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio.  Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics, state, or environment and 2) produce empathic, human-like responses that achieve conversational or task-oriented objectives.   

  • Design model architectures, training schemes, and inference algorithms that are adapted for hardware at the bare metal enabling cost efficient training on billion-hour datasets and powering real-time inference for hundreds of millions of concurrent conversations.

The Challenge

We are seeking researchers who:

  • See "unsolved" problems as opportunities to pioneer entirely new approaches

  • Can identify the one critical experiment that will validate or kill an idea in days, not months

  • Have the vision to scale successful proofs-of-concept 100x

  • Are obsessed with using AI to automate and amplify your own impact

If you find yourself energized rather than daunted by these expectations—if you're already thinking about five ideas to try while reading this—you might be the researcher we need. This role demands obsession with the problems, creativity in approach, and relentless drive toward elegant, scalable solutions. The technical challenges are immense, but the potential impact is transformative.


It's Important to Us That You Have

  • Strong mathematical foundation in statistical learning theory, particularly in areas relevant to self-supervised and multimodal learning

  • Deep expertise in foundation model architectures, with an understanding of how to scale training across multiple modalities

  • Proven ability to bridge theory and practice—someone who can both derive novel mathematical formulations and implement them efficiently

  • Demonstrated ability to build data pipelines that can process and curate massive datasets while maintaining quality and diversity

  • Track record of designing controlled experiments that isolate the impact of architectural innovations and validate theoretical insights

  • Experience optimizing models for real-world deployment, including knowledge of hardware constraints and efficiency techniques

  • History of open-source contributions or research publications that have advanced the state of the art in speech/language AI


Ideal Researcher Profile

An ideal researcher, as evidenced by the recurring themes across these foundational papers, excels in five key areas: (1) Statistical & Mathematical Foundations, (2) Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation, (3) Data-Driven & Scalable Systems, (4) Hardware & Systems Understanding, and (5) Rigorous Experimental Design. Below is a synthesis of how each paper highlights these qualities, with references illustrating why they matter for building robust, impactful deep learning models.



1. Statistical & Mathematical Foundations

Mastery of Core Concepts

Many papers, like Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models and Neural Discrete Representation Learning (VQ-VAE), reflect the importance of power-law analyses, derivation of novel losses, or adaptation of fundamental equations (e.g., in VQ-VAE's commitment loss or rectified flows in Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers). Such mathematical grounding clarifies why models converge or suffer collapse.

Combining Existing Theories in Novel Ways

Papers such as Moshi (combining text modeling, audio codecs, and hierarchical generative modeling) and Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ's adaptation of classic scalar quantization to replace vector-quantized representations) show how reusing but reimagining known techniques can yield breakthroughs. Many references (e.g., the structured state-space duality in Transformers are SSMs) underscore how unifying previously separate research lines can reveal powerful algorithmic or theoretical insights.

Logical Reasoning and Assumption Testing

Across all papers—particularly in the problem statements of Whisper or Rectified Flow Transformers—the authors present assumptions (e.g., "scaling data leads to zero-shot robustness" or "straight-line noise injection improves sample efficiency") and systematically verify them with thorough empirical results. An ideal researcher similarly grounds new ideas in well-formed, testable hypotheses.


2. Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation

Creative Solutions to Known Bottlenecks

Each paper puts forth a unique algorithmic contribution—Rectified Flow Transformers redefines standard diffusion paths, FSQ proposes simpler scalar quantizations contrasted with VQ, phi-3 mini relies on curated data and blocksparse attention, and Mamba-2 merges SSM speed with attention concepts.

Turning Theory into Practice

Whether it's the direct preference optimization (DPO) for alignment in phi-3 or the residual vector quantization in SoundStream, these works show that bridging design insights with implementable prototypes is essential.

Clear Impact Through Prototypes & Open-Source

Many references (Whisper, neural discrete representation learning, Mamba-2) highlight releasing code or pretrained models, enabling the broader community to replicate and build upon new methods. This premise of collaboration fosters faster progress.


3. Data-Driven & Scalable Systems

Emphasis on Large-Scale Data and Efficient Pipelines

Papers such as Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision (Whisper) and BASE TTS demonstrate that collecting and processing hundreds of thousands of hours of real-world audio can unlock new capabilities in zero-shot or low-resource domains. Meanwhile, phi-3 Technical Report shows that filtering and curating data at scale (e.g., "data optimal regime") can yield high performance even in smaller models.

Strategic Use of Data for Staged Training

A recurring strategy is to vary sources of data or the order of tasks. Whisper trains on multilingual tasks, BASE TTS uses subsets/stages for pretraining on speech tokens, and phi-3 deploys multiple training phases (web data, then synthetic data). This systematic approach to data underscores how an ideal researcher designs training curricula and data filtering protocols for maximum performance.


4. Hardware & Systems Understanding

Efficient Implementations at Scale

Many works illustrate how researchers tune architectures for modern accelerators: the In-Datacenter TPU paper exemplifies domain-specific hardware design for dense matrix multiplications, while phi-3 leverages blocksparse attention and custom Triton kernels to run advanced LLMs on resource-limited devices.

Real-Time & On-Device Constraints

SoundStream shows how to compress audio in real time on a smartphone CPU, demonstrating that knowledge of hardware constraints (latency, limited memory) drives design choices. Similarly, Moshi's low-latency streaming TTS and phi-3-mini's phone-based inference highlight that an ideal researcher must adapt algorithms to resource limits while maintaining robustness.

Architectural & Optimization Details

Papers like Mamba-2 in Transformers are SSMs and the In-Datacenter TPU work show how exploiting specialized matrix decomposition, custom memory hierarchies, or quantization approaches can lead to breakthroughs in speed or energy efficiency.


5. Rigorous Experimental Design

Controlled Comparisons & Ablations

Nearly all papers—Whisper, FSQ, Mamba-2, BASE TTS—use systematic ablations to isolate the impact of individual components (e.g., ablation on vector-quantization vs. scalar quantization in FSQ, or size of codebooks in VQ-VAEs). This approach reveals which design decisions truly matter.

Multifold Evaluation Metrics

From MUSHRA listening tests (SoundStream, BASE TTS) to FID in image synthesis (Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers, FSQ) to perplexity or zero-shot generalization in language (phi-3, Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models), the works demonstrate the value of comprehensive, carefully chosen metrics.

Stress Tests & Edge Cases

Whisper's out-of-distribution speech benchmarks, SoundStream's evaluation on speech + music, or Mamba-2's performance on multi-query associative recall demonstrate the importance of specialized challenge sets. Researchers who craft or adopt rigorous benchmarks and "red-team" their models (as in phi-3 safety alignment) are better prepared to address real-world complexities.



Summary

Overall, an ideal researcher in deep learning consistently demonstrates:

  • A solid grounding in theoretical and statistical principles

  • A talent for proposing and validating new algorithmic solutions

  • The capacity to orchestrate data pipelines that scale and reflect real-world diversity

  • Awareness of hardware constraints and system-level trade-offs for efficiency

  • Thorough and transparent experimental practices

These qualities surface across research on speech (Whisper, BASE TTS), language modeling (Scaling Laws, phi-3), specialized hardware (TPU, Transformers are SSMs), and new representation methods (VQ-VAE, FSQ, SoundStream). By balancing these attributes—rigorous math, innovative algorithms, large-scale data engineering, hardware-savvy optimizations, and reproducible experimentation—researchers can produce impactful, trustworthy advancements in foundational deep learning.




Foundational Papers

title: People Director
description:
Zibber groeit. In Nederland, België en Duitsland, en met verdere Europese ambities. Dat vraagt om een People Director die zorgt dat onze organisatie kan meegroeien: met stevige & mensgerichte leiders, de juiste mensen op de juiste plek, een high-performance cultuur en People-processen die ons helpen om beter en sneller te werken.

We zoeken een strategische en hands-on People leader die gelooft dat duurzame groei begint bij mensen. Iemand die oog heeft voor wat onze collega's en leiders nodig hebben om met Zibber mee te groeien, zich te ontwikkelen én met plezier goed werk te kunnen doen. Je verbindt die menselijke kant aan onze bedrijfsstrategie en kijkt verder dan wat vandaag nodig is. Zo bouw je aan de organisatie die Zibber de komende drie tot vijf jaar nodig heeft, zonder het ondernemerschap, de persoonlijke aandacht en de energie kwijt te raken die ons succesvol hebben gemaakt.

Over Zibber

Zibber helpt vastgoedprofessionals zoals makelaars, bedrijfsmakelaars, woningcorporaties en property managers om woningen en panden beter, sneller en professioneler in de markt te zetten. Dat doen we met vastgoedfotografie, video, plattegronden, 3D-laserscanning en meetrapporten.

Onze kracht zit in de combinatie van mensen, operatie en technologie. Met ons eigen platform MyZibber digitaliseren en automatiseren we een groot deel van het proces voor onze klanten. Technologie, data en AI spelen daarbij een steeds grotere rol in hoe we werken en groeien.

Met circa 250 collega's in Nederland, België en Duitsland zijn we marktleider in vastgoedmedia. Het overgrote deel van onze mensen werkt in het veld: bijna 200 collega's leveren dagelijks op locatie bij onze klanten. We zijn PE-backed en werken gericht op groei, professionalisering, schaalbaarheid en internationale expansie. People & Culture speelt daarin een sleutelrol.

De rol

Als People Director ben je eindverantwoordelijk voor People & Culture over heel Zibber: Nederland, België en Duitsland. Je bent onderdeel van het managementteam en rapporteert rechtstreeks aan de CEO. De volgende fase vraagt om een grotere en meer strategische rol. 

Je belangrijkste opdracht is ervoor te zorgen dat Zibber én onze mensen klaar zijn voor de volgende groeifase. Je bouwt aan een omgeving waarin collega's zich gezien voelen, zich kunnen ontwikkelen en verantwoordelijkheid nemen. Je helpt leiders om hun teams daarin mee te nemen en vertaalt onze bedrijfsstrategie naar een heldere People-agenda, zodat mensen, organisatie en ambities samen kunnen groeien.

Wat deze rol anders maakt dan een standaard People-rol: onze vraag is seizoensgebonden en beweegt mee met de woningmarkt, en onze organisatie is grotendeels een verspreide buitendienst. Capaciteitsplanning, de bijbehorende kostencyclus en on- en offboarding op grote schaal vormen de kern van je werk.

Je focus ligt op vier gebieden:

1.Organisatie en leiderschap

  • Je bent een gelijkwaardige en onafhankelijke gesprekspartner voor de CEO, het MT en de leidinggevenden op organisatiestructuur, leiderschap, verandering en organisatie-effectiviteit.

  • Je zorgt ervoor dat structuur, rollen, governance en leiderschap de strategie ondersteunen, zodat de organisatie sneller en effectiever resultaten behaalt.

  • Je ontwikkelt de leiderschapscultuur verder en helpt managers sterke teams bouwen die groeien en leveren.

  • Je brengt een helder People-perspectief in, stelt vragen die de organisatie verder helpen en maakt met de board en het MT duidelijke keuzes.

  • Je onderhoudt de relatie met de medezeggenschap in Nederland, België en Duitsland en betrekt hen tijdig en constructief bij verandering.

2. Buitendienst, performance en talent

  • Je professionaliseert workforce planning voor een seizoensgebonden, verspreide buitendienst: capaciteitsplanning, high-volume recruitment, on- en offboarding op grote schaal en retentie in het veld.

  • Je stuurt actief op de kostenkant van die cyclus en maakt de formatie- en kostenimpact van People-beslissingen inzichtelijk.

  • Je zorgt voor gezond, veilig en duurzaam werken in het veld, en voor een goed mobiliteits- en leasevlootbeleid voor de buitendienst.

  • Je bouwt aan een cultuur waarin mensen weten wat er van hen verwacht wordt, elkaar feedback geven en ruimte krijgen om te groeien.

  • Je professionaliseert performance management, talentmanagement, succession planning en leiderschapsontwikkeling.

  • Je zorgt voor een sterke employee experience, een omgeving waarin mensen graag werken én goed presteren.

3. Schaalbare en toekomstbestendige People-infrastructuur

  • Je zorgt ervoor dat People-processen, systemen en governance eenvoudig, efficiënt en schaalbaar zijn.

  • Je richt onze flexibele schil en buitendienst arbeidsrechtelijk robuust en toekomstbestendig in, inclusief kwalificatievraagstukken rondom zelfstandigheid. Je voert hierop de regie en werkt samen met gespecialiseerde arbeidsrechtelijke adviseurs in de drie landen.

  • Je bent verantwoordelijk voor compensation & benefits, arbeidsvoorwaarden en het People-budget.

  • Je maakt People-data inzichtelijk en gebruikt analytics voor betere beslissingen over formatie, verloop, engagement, recruitment en performance.

  • Je zet HR-tech, AI en automation slim in om de People-organisatie effectiever en schaalbaarder te maken.

4. Cultuur en change

  • Je zorgt ervoor dat Happiness, Keep it Simple en Get it Done zichtbaar blijven in hoe we werken, leidinggeven en besluiten nemen. Juist ook als de organisatie groter en internationaler wordt.

  • Je helpt de organisatie professionaliseren zonder onnodige bureaucratie.

  • Bij groei, integraties en veranderingen help je bewust bouwen aan één Zibber: met dezelfde uitgangspunten voor cultuur en leiderschap, maar met ruimte voor wat lokaal anders moet.

  • Je bouwt samen met Marketing aan onze employer value proposition en employer branding, voor twee verschillende arbeidsmarkten: de buitendienst en het kantoor- en technologietalent.

  • Je stuurt het People-team aan, ontwikkelt het verder en zorgt voor duidelijke rollen, eigenaarschap en hoge kwaliteit.

Leiderschap bij Zibber

Als People Director geef je zelf het voorbeeld. Je maakt complexiteit simpel, creëert duidelijkheid en geeft mensen eigenaarschap. Je combineert hoge standaarden met oprechte aandacht voor mensen.

Je creëert ruimte voor verschillende perspectieven en durft besluiten te nemen wanneer dat nodig is. Je brengt een onafhankelijk perspectief in, luistert naar andere inzichten en spreekt je uit wanneer dat nodig is. Je kijkt verder dan People & Culture, doorbreekt silo's en neemt met het MT verantwoordelijkheid voor het resultaat van Zibber als geheel.

Strategisch wanneer het kan. Handen uit de mouwen wanneer het moet.

Wat je krijgt

Je komt terecht in een club die hard werkt en net zo hard lacht. Happiness is niet voor niets een van onze kernwaarden: we nemen het werk serieus en onszelf wat minder. Verder krijg je:

  • Een ambitieus en informeel team met veel energie en humor, waar successen worden gevierd en een goede grap nooit ver weg is.

  • Een sleutelpositie op directieniveau binnen een snelgroeiende internationale organisatie, met een plek in het MT en directe samenwerking met de CEO.

  • Volledige ownership over de People & Culture-agenda en directe invloed op hoe Zibber zich de komende jaren organiseert.

  • Korte lijnen, snelle besluitvorming en veel verantwoordelijkheid, in een PE-backed omgeving met ambitie en duidelijke groeidoelen.

  • De ruimte om technologie, data, AI en automation actief in te zetten binnen People & Culture.

  • Een vast salaris tussen €7.000 en €8.500 bruto per maand op basis van 40 uur, aangevuld met een bonus gekoppeld aan People- en bedrijfsresultaten.

  • Een keuzebudget voor extra vakantiedagen of extra pensioeninleg.

  • Een thuiswerkvergoeding voor de dagen dat je thuis werkt.

title: Working Student - Field & Event Marketing (m/f/d)
description:
The role

We're looking for a Working Student - Field & Event Marketing (m/f/d) to own our events from first plan to final follow-up. Our event marketing activity is ramping up, and needs an owner. 

From November 2026, that's you: you coordinate every trade show and conference we attend, including social promotion, so that each one drives market awareness and sales pipeline.

You'll work closely with our GTM team, preferably 16-20 hours a week during the semester, for at least 12 months. 


Why you'll love this role

  • Real ownership: You get the goal and the budget for each event.
  • Direct impact: Every show you run turns into leads and meetings for our sales team.
  • Hands-on experience: Trade fairs, vendors, logistics, social content and CRM, all in one.
  • Industry exposure: See up close how a startup sells into biotech, pharma and chemistry.
  • Events covered: Travel, accommodation and per diems are paid for every event you join.


Your mission

  • Plan the calendar: Build our 2027 event calendar, with cost and rationale for every event.
  • Run events end to end: Booth, freight, print, swag and travel, including German vendors and venues.
  • Social Promotion: Promo and live coverage published on LinkedIn for that show, with a performance report delivered afterwards. Post-event content ships within 5 working days of every show.
  • Close the loop: Every lead scanned at a show goes into Attio within 48 hours.
  • Build the playbook: Cost, leads and meetings per event, so we know which shows are worth going back to. Document how each event runs, so the next one is easier.
  • Keep stock in check: Booth assets, swag and print tracked, so nothing gets rush-ordered the week before.
  • Be there: Join some of the events you planned on site.


Your profile

  • Enrolment: Enrolled at a university in Munich, at least until the end of winter semester 2027/28.
  • Languages: Fluent German (B2+) and English (C1+). Vendors, venues and invoices are mostly German; everything we publish is in English.
  • Organization: You've run something with moving parts and a deadline, where other people depended on you.
  • Ownership: You chase the details nobody assigned you. The shipment that hasn't arrived yet is yours.
  • Public presence: You're comfortable representing UniteLabs on a booth floor and on LinkedIn.


Nice to have

  • Life-science exposure: a lab job, a research placement, a biotech-adjacent degree
  • Has staffed a booth or run a student conference
  • Has grown a social account and can show what worked
  • Driver's license
  • Canva, Figma, or basic video editing skills
  • Fluent with AI tools for research and drafting


How to apply

Send us your CV and 3 to 5 sentences about the most complicated thing you've organized: what had to happen, what went wrong, and what you did about it. Add your expected graduation date in the application form.
