WHY JOIN US?

We are winners of the prestigious Culture 100 award that recognises the most loved and happiest tech companies to work for! We have just raised $52m in funding led by global venture capital firm Bessemer Venture Partners (an early backer of LinkedIn and Shopify) to accelerate our growth plans!

As pioneers, we’re always driving for new territory and positive change, so our work as a group is never done. Where others see difficulty, it’s our responsibility to see possibility – building new experiences, launching new titles and listening to drivers.

Being a part of Carwow Group means championing drivers and the automotive industry, acting as a disrupter and never being afraid to fail (but learning fast when we do!).

Our team of 600 employees across the UK, Germany, Spain and Portugal are revolutionising car-changing and we are fast expanding our mission across every single brand and country we operate in, so jump in!


THE ROLE

This is a director role running the operating engine behind our commercial teams. Carwow sells cars in two ways: Sell My Car, where drivers sell their car to dealers, and Get Your Car, where they buy or lease their next one. As Director, GTM & Revenue Operations you own the operating model those commercial teams run on: the go-to-market process, the enablement and quality that get people productive, the systems they work in (Salesforce and the wider commercial tech stack), the analytics that forecast the commercial number, and the programme management that lands cross-functional change. The function covers five areas: GTM Operations, Sales Enablement, Tooling & Platform, Rev-Ops Analytics and Program Management. You report to the VP, Marketplace Operations and sit close to both the numbers and the commercial teams you serve. You make the commercial motion work; the commercial teams own the selling and the relationships.

This is a builder's role as much as a running one. You inherit a team of three (programme management, sales enablement and platform) and a clear mandate to grow the function to what the business needs. Shaping and hiring that team, and making the case for it, is central to the job. The commercial org has recently brought its Sell My Car and Get Your Car teams into a single account-management function serving one dealer network, so you'll run one operating model across both products (a unified Salesforce, aligned targets and comp, consistent enablement and quality) and get the last of that integration to steady state. The function has already moved real numbers here, reworking the sales process, standing up sales-engagement tooling and sharpening enablement, and your job is to take that further.

You own the operating model, process, enablement, the systems requirement and the forecast. The commercial organisation owns the relationships, the selling and delivery against the number. You design the targets, compensation and territory structures with commercial leadership and you shape decisions through the strength of the operating case. In your first year, success looks like a forecast that's trusted and accurate, new hires productive faster, a consistent quality bar across the combined team, and the platform and process the org runs on every day.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

You will own the commercial operating model and the team that runs it, working hand in glove with the commercial organisation, Workforce Management, the trading leads, and the analytics and data teams that support the whole function.

  • Own GTM operations: define the go-to-market playbook, pipeline and commercial process across both marketplaces, and, with commercial leadership, design the targets, compensation and territory / account structures that tie individual attainment to the business outcome. Own capacity and headcount planning with Workforce Management.

  • Own sales enablement and quality: build the onboarding and ramp-to-productivity structures, a standard readiness sign-off, org-wide QA and calibration, and ongoing L&D for both individual contributors and leaders, so new hires get productive faster and quality holds across the organisation.

  • Own the requirements for the commercial systems and tooling: direct Salesforce as the commercial system of record, owning the process and workflow design, prioritisation and the roadmap to bring the whole commercial org onto one platform, plus the sales-engagement and automation tooling (e.g. Groove), AI-assisted workflows and the performance dashboards the teams run on. You own the requirement and how the commercial org runs on the platform; the platform itself, its build and administration, sits with the tech org, who you partner with and direct.

  • Own revenue-operations analytics and forecasting: produce a forward-looking commercial forecast that feeds trading and reconciles to Finance's P&L view, own the operational reporting that diagnoses what the volume and operational teams are driving into the number, and provide the evidence base behind comp and performance decisions. You own the operational read and set the requirement; you partner with Finance and the central analytics and data teams, who own the build.

  • Own program management: run the commercial PMO, from end-to-end discovery and sizing of new initiatives through governance (charters, RACI, risk and impact), so cross-functional commercial programmes land on time with clear ownership.

  • Build the function: shape and hire the team the function needs across the five areas, from a starting base of three, and make the case for the investment. Run the combined Sell My Car and Get Your Car commercial operation as one, a single dealer view, one operating model, and consistent process across both products.

  • Get more out of the team with AI and automation: mature how the commercial org operates with AI-first tooling and automation, so manual workflows disappear and the org gets the answer without a person in the loop.

  • Feed the operating rhythm: own the commercial-motion input into the weekly operating cadence and the read up to Finance, trading and the CEO, with a clean, leadership-ready view of where the pipeline sits and where it is heading.


WHAT YOU’LL NEED

Please note: We know that no candidate will be a perfect match for everything here, so please apply if you're close to the brief. If you meet most of the essentials, we'd like to hear from you.

The essentials:

  • A track record of leading a revenue-operations, commercial-operations or GTM-operations function at scale, in a marketplace, growth or B2B sales context

  • Breadth across the operating model: you've owned, or closely partnered on, most of GTM process, enablement, commercial systems and analytics, and you understand how they fit together

  • Strong CRM fluency with Salesforce as a system of record: you can set the requirements, shape the data model and process, and direct a platform team, not just keep it clean

  • Commercial process and incentive design: targets, compensation, territory and capacity planning tied to business outcomes

  • A people leader and builder: you've grown a multi-disciplinary team from a small base, hired well, and set a clear bar

  • Analytical and data-fluent: comfortable in a forecast and a pipeline model, and drawing honest conclusions from the numbers

How you'll work (we'll explore these in interview):

  • Fluent and curious with AI: you use it to work faster and help a team adopt it

  • Credible with senior stakeholders: you make a well-evidenced case and hold it under challenge, and you influence across teams you don't own

Nice to have:

  • SQL / data warehouse fluency

  • Marketplace, two-sided platform or automotive experience

INTERVIEW PROCESS

The mission

You will be the reference point for the most complex hardware interventions across our sites.

Mistral's compute is our largest investment and the foundation of frontier AI in Europe. As a Senior Data Center Hardware Engineer (L4-L5), you own the interventions that require the highest level of technical expertise: multi-node failures in production, full-rack deployments of GPU-dense systems, and vendor escalations where you speak as the technical authority for our sites.

You'll work end-to-end — compute, storage, interconnect, power and cooling interfaces — across our data center footprint, raising the bar on reliability as our capacity grows. This is a hands-on senior IC role: deep technical leadership and mentorship, no direct line management.

Location: Based at one of our data centers in the Paris region, with occasional visits to our other sites as needed.

 

What you'll do

  • Lead complex interventions — vendor-level and multi-node operations in production: full rack builds and bring-up, GPU-dense platform deployment (H100/H200-class and next-gen, including liquid-cooled racks), intricate recabling, post-restart diagnosis. You own the plan, the risk assessment, and the rollback.

  • Own vendor management — coordinate repairs, part replacements and escalations directly with hardware vendors; hold them to their SLAs; drive proactive fixes from failure trends.

  • Diagnose at depth — correlate symptoms across compute, storage, interconnect and cooling; read BMC/IPMI consoles, OS logs and crash dumps; methodical root-cause analysis that ends in concrete corrective actions.

  • Deploy and validate — structured bring-up and validation of new racks and platforms; work with networking and infrastructure teams to take installations from delivery to production-ready.

  • Lift the team — mentor and pair with L1–L3 engineers on live operations; turn your knowledge into SOPs, checklists and training material; propose and build small automation (Python/Bash) to shorten MTTR.

  • Work the facility interface — partner with critical facilities/engineering ops on power, cooling (air and liquid), PDU and monitoring (BMS/EPMS) boundaries; enforce ESD/LOTO/PPE and audit-ready change discipline everywhere.

  • Own spares & reliability — plan spares strategy, track fleet failure trends, and run proactive vendor actions before incidents happen.

 

About you

  • 6+ years in data center / server hardware or L2/L3 hardware support, including complex hands-on work in production environments (HPC/AI/cloud at scale strongly preferred).

  • End-to-end hardware expertise: CPU/memory/PCIe (incl. accelerators), NICs, PSUs, drives, network, power and cooling interfaces (DLC included); strong judgment on when and how to escalate.

  • Diagnostics depth: confident with BMC/IPMI logs, Linux logs and CLI checks; structured root-cause analysis.

  • Deployment experience: you've taken racks from delivery to production, with concrete examples to show for it.

  • Vendor fluency: you've managed hardware vendors — RMAs, field replacements, escalations — to concrete outcomes.

  • Impeccable safety and discipline: ESD/LOTO/PPE without exception; clean, labeled, auditable work.

  • Communication & mentoring: clear status updates and handovers; able to coach engineers during live incidents with composure.

  • Mobility: willing to visit our other sites in the Paris region as needed.

 

Nice to have

  • GPU-dense platform experience: NVIDIA H-series (H100/H200) or GB-series rack deployments.

  • High-speed interconnects (InfiniBand/RoCE), RAID/storage (NVMe/SAS/SATA), vendor tooling (iDRAC/iLO/IPMI).

Founded in 2012, Mirakl has been at the forefront of marketplace innovation, empowering every business to compete in the platform economy.

Today, Mirakl's operating system combines an enterprise marketplace solution (Mirakl Platform) that enables retailers and B2B organizations to launch, scale, and operate marketplaces and dropship, AI-powered multichannel selling (Mirakl Connect), retail media (Mirakl Ads) and an agentic commerce infrastructure (Mirakl Nexus).

You'll be part of our EMEA Solution Consulting team led by Jonathan D'Elissagaray, Director of Solution Consulting. Mirakl Connect is Mirakl's ecosystem platform, connecting marketplace operators and sellers to simplify partnerships, onboarding, and growth. description:

About this position:

Role Overview 

We are looking for a Single Photon Source Lithography Engineer to support the development, stabilization and industrialization of our semiconductor fabrication processes. 

At our current stage of maturity, this position combines advanced process development, hands-on R&D and manufacturing engineering. The Lithography Engineer will play a key role in bridging the gap between Advanced R&D and Production, transforming newly developed process building blocks into robust, repeatable and scalable manufacturing processes. 

The role will have a strong focus on in-situ localization of quantum dots (QDs) at cryogenic temperatures and laser lithography over the localized Qds with laser writing techniques. The successful candidate will work closely with R&D teams, fabrication engineers, equipment owners and cleanroom operators to improve process capability, reproducibility, yield and production throughput. 

This is a highly hands-on position requiring a strong understanding of semiconductor fabrication, rigorous experimental methodology and the ability to investigate complex interactions between process parameters and device performance. 

Key Responsibilities 

Process Development & Industrialization 

  • Develop, optimize and stabilize QD positioning and laser lithography process. 
  • Contribute to the development of GUIs and automation codes in the Python programming language. 
  • Contrinute to the development of fully-automated QD-positioning and litography tools. 
  • Validate and qualify new fabrication equipment and associated processes. 
  • Define process windows, recipes, operating conditions and acceptance criteria. 
  • Use structured experimentation, including Design of Experiments (DoE) where appropriate, to understand process sensitivities and optimize performance. 
  • Improve process repeatability, reproducibility, robustness and within-wafer / wafer-to-wafer homogeneity. 
  • Prepare processes and equipment for increasing wafer sizes, batch sizes and production volumes. 

R&D to Production Transfer 

  • Act as a key technical interface between Advanced R&D and Production. 
  • Convert R&D process building blocks into stable, documented and manufacturable processes. 
  • Assess manufacturability, scalability and process risks before transfer to production. 
  • Define qualification plans and acceptance criteria before releasing new or modified processes to production. 
  • Lead or contribute to Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (PFMEA) for critical fabrication steps, identifying potential failure modes, their effects on device performance and appropriate prevention and control measures. 
  • Translate PFMEA outcomes into process controls, monitoring plans, acceptance criteria, Control Plans and documentation. 
  • Support technology transfer through clear documentation, operator training and technical communication. 

Process Control & Yield Improvement 

  • Monitor and improve production process performance, yield and throughput. 
  • Establish regular process checks, controls and monitoring methodologies, including Statistical Process Control (SPC) where relevant. 
  • Detect process drifts, investigate deviations and define corrective and preventive actions. 
  • Lead root-cause analysis and troubleshooting activities for yield losses, process excursions and equipment-related issues. 
  • Define and maintain relevant process KPIs and contribute to continuous-improvement initiatives. 
  • Promote best practices that increase process stability, repeatability and equipment utilization. 

Equipment & Production Support 

  • Provide hands-on technical support to cleanroom operators and production teams. 
  • Work closely with equipment suppliers and internal teams to resolve technical issues. 
  • Contribute to a safe, disciplined and efficient cleanroom environment. 

Process Characterization & Data Analysis 

  • Correlate process data with structural, optical and electrical characterization results. 
  • Use experimental data to identify process sensitivities, failure mechanisms and optimization opportunities. 
  • Develop appropriate data-analysis tools to support process monitoring and engineering decisions. 
  • Search and analyze scientific and technical literature to support process development and troubleshooting. 

Documentation & Communication 

  • Create and maintain high-quality process documentation, including process specifications, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), equipment recipes, qualification reports, Control Plans, process-development reports and troubleshooting guides. 
  • Ensure frequent and clear reporting of process status, experimental results, risks and improvement actions. 
  • Communicate effectively with colleagues from different technical backgrounds and levels of experience. 
  • Train and support operators and other team members on new or updated processes. 

Requirements

Required Qualifications & Experience 

  • Master's degree or PhD in Optics, Materials Science, Physics, Micro/Nanotechnology, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. 
  • Hands-on experience with semiconductor or photonic-device fabrication in a cleanroom environment. 
  • Hands-on experience in conception, assembling, and alignment of optical systems. 
  • Hands-on experience in conception, assembling, and operation of electronic devices 
  • Python programming language fluency. 
  • Excellent attention to detail and a rigorous approach to experimental work. 
  • Strong troubleshooting, root-cause analysis and problem-solving skills. 
  • Ability to independently investigate technical problems using experimental data and scientific literature. 
  • Strong communication and documentation skills. 
  • Fluent English, both written and spoken. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience in developments of GUIs with the python programming language. 
  • Experience in a semiconductor manufacturing, pilot-line or production environment. 
  • Experience with process industrialization and transfer from R&D to production. 
  • Experience with PFMEA, Control Plans, SPC, DoE or other structured process-risk and continuous-improvement methodologies. 
  • Experience with III-V semiconductor devices, particularly AlGaAs-based photonic structures, resonators or VCSEL-type technologies. 

Profile 

We are looking for someone who combines the mindset of an R&D engineer with the rigor of a manufacturing/process engineer. 

The ideal candidate is comfortable developing new systems where all parameters are not yet fully understood, while also being able to transform experimental processes into stable, controlled and documented production workflows. 

You should enjoy working directly in the cleanroom, analyzing data, developing Python projects, solving complex fabrication problems and collaborating across R&D and production teams.

description:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The Role

Heidi sits in an unusual position. We lead a category being built for the first time. Hundreds of thousands of clinicians found us on their own, started using the product for free, and told a colleague. The market is open, and we're in the privileged position of clinicians already liking the product. Your job is to turn those smaller-scale use cases into enterprise deals.

You're the first line to Heidi in France. Inbound demand connects you with cabinets, maisons de santé, and hospital groups already using us, and you decide whether to qualify each one in, out, or close it yourself. Where the signals run thin, you build the outbound.

For most clinicians, you'll be the first person from Heidi they ever speak to. You'll both triage inbound to Account Executives where needed and close your own deals from day one, because we want people as close to the frontline as possible. You'll build a network across French healthcare that outlasts the role.

What you’ll do

  • Work the inbound queue and the warm product signals across France. Your day goes to clinicians and cabinets already using Heidi, where the product tells you who's outgrown the free version.

  • Build outbound where the signals are thin: pick the practice groups, maisons de santé and hospital groups worth going after and work them in French.

  • Research the accounts behind those signals, work out who else in the cabinet or hospital group needs to be in the conversation, and build the case for each one.

  • Reach the people the signals point to, across calls, email and social, while the interest is still fresh.

  • Book demos and meetings for your AEs with enough context that nothing is lost in the handoff.

  • Own SMB deals end to end, from first conversation through to closed.

  • Keep HubSpot accurate, keep the pipeline moving and hit your qualified-lead number every month.

  • Partner with AEs, Marketing, Product, Operations and Customer Success so what you promise on the call matches what clinicians get, and so the French-language product and collateral keep up with what you hear.

  • Track what's shifting in French healthcare (regulation, the practice and hospital groups, Assurance Maladie and the mutuelles, the competitive set) and tell the team what you're hearing on the phones.

What you'll need

  • Native or fluent French, and English that allows you to work in a global team.

  • You've worked somewhere with a high bar, whether that's tech, sales, creative, banking, consulting, or PE/VC. We care more about what you've achieved than your time in a sales role.

  • You care about what we do. You'd rather learn how the product works than memorise a pitch.

  • You can hold a conversation with anyone and get to the point of it fast. Clinicians have extremely busy schedules, so you need to respect that and still get the meeting.

  • Knowing how French healthcare buys (who decides in a cabinet, a maison de santé or a hospital group, and who pays) is a head start. If you don't know it yet, you're the type who'd learn it in your first weeks.

  • Organised and self-running. You run your own list, your own day and your own follow-ups without being chased.

  • Passion for AI, shown through hands-on building, prototyping or side projects.

  • You default to building over requesting.

  • You're confident in your thinking and open to being wrong. At Heidi, great ideas win regardless of who surfaces them.

Attitude is more important than experience, so if you are a hungry, competitive and highly motivated operator who has a knack for problem-solving and building relationships, we want to hear from you.

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

We take care of you.

We chose to open-source our benefits hub, if you care to take a peek.

We need a builder who owns the complete production outcome — not a prompt tinkerer, not a researcher, not a PM who delegates the build.

Requirements:

  • Strong record of building and shipping production software end-to-end, ideally in a SaaS, marketplace, or workflow product — with real users and real revenue on the line.

Interview Process

  2. Working Interview – Financial Controller (90 min): A live case using real, anonymised material from our own administration, plus a short take-home assignment (capped at 3 hours, and paid).

title: Computer Vision & AI Engineer - Interceptor C‑UAS (m/f/d)

About the role:

At Quantum Systems, we are building highly autonomous interceptor systems that must perceive, decide, and act under extreme latency, motion, and environmental constraints.

We are looking for a Computer Vision & AI Engineer to drive the perception stack of our Counter-UAS interceptor platform. You will work on low-latency camera pipelines, small-object detection, object tracking, sensor fusion, visual odometry, precision landing, camera calibration, embedded inference, and data pipelines for training and validation.

This role is suited for someone with a strong academic or practical background in computer vision, AI, robotics, or perception systems. A Master’s degree is expected; a PhD is a strong plus. We are open to ambitious early-career candidates if they bring strong technical depth, practical implementation skills, and the ability to own complex perception problems.

Your Mission

You will develop the vision and AI pipeline that turns raw camera data into actionable perception outputs for autonomous flight. This includes low-latency detection and tracking, motion-aware vision, sensor fusion with inertial data, 3D direction-vector estimation, GPS-denied navigation, and precision landing support.


What is your Day to Day Mission:

  • Bring up, optimize, and maintain high-performance camera pipelines, including CSI camera interfaces, raw image access, buffering, synchronization, and latency reduction.

  • Develop detection algorithms for small and difficult-to-see objects in moving and rotating camera images.

  • Combine machine learning and classical computer vision approaches where appropriate.

  • Fuse inertial data, motion information, and visual data to improve detection and tracking in moving image sequences.

  • Build object tracking pipelines that can switch from initial detection to low-latency tracking once a target has been acquired.

  • Optimize perception pipelines for embedded execution on NVIDIA Jetson platforms.

  • Work toward high frame-rate processing targets in the range of 100–300 FPS, where technically feasible.

  • Use camera intrinsics and extrinsics to transform image-space detections into 3D direction vectors or other navigation-relevant outputs.

  • Work on GPS-denied navigation concepts using visual odometry, including approaches with forward-facing camera views rather than only downward-looking cameras.

  • Develop visual support for precision landing, including height estimation, velocity estimation, and motion-state estimation from limited camera perspectives.

  • Build and maintain the data pipeline from onboard recordings to cloud storage, preprocessing, annotation, dataset generation, training, validation, and benchmarking.

  • Work with annotation tools such as SuperAnnotate, CVAT, Label Studio, or comparable systems.

  • Benchmark and evaluate different model and algorithm families, including approaches such as CenterNet, SuperPoint, SuperGlue, optical flow, feature tracking, object detection, and lightweight embedded models.

  • Build deployment pipelines using ONNX, TensorRT, custom inference runners, or comparable embedded inference tooling.

  • Collaborate closely with autonomy, flight control, embedded software, test, and systems engineering teams.




What you bring to the team:

  • Master’s degree or PhD in computer vision, AI, robotics, machine learning, electrical engineering, computer science, aerospace engineering, or a comparable technical field.

  • Strong understanding of computer vision fundamentals, camera geometry, feature detection, object detection, tracking, calibration, and image-space to 3D transformations.

  • Practical experience implementing computer vision or machine learning pipelines in Python and C++.

  • Experience with embedded inference, ideally on NVIDIA Jetson, CUDA, TensorRT, ONNX, GStreamer, V4L2, or similar technologies.

  • Ability to read, understand, and implement ideas from current research papers.

  • Understanding of latency, throughput, profiling, memory movement, and real-time constraints.

  • Experience with dataset creation, annotation workflows, training/validation splits, metrics, and benchmarking.

  • Strong mathematical intuition and willingness to debug both algorithms and real-world sensor data.

  • Ability to take ownership of a technical area and drive it from research prototype to flight-test-ready software.

    • Experience with UAV perception, robotics perception, visual odometry, SLAM, sensor fusion, or tracking systems.

    • Experience with IMU-camera fusion, ego-motion compensation, rolling-shutter effects, or high-frame-rate cameras.

    • Experience with precision landing, visual navigation, or GPS-denied navigation.

    • Experience building cloud-based ML training and validation pipelines.

    • Publications, thesis work, GitHub projects, demos, or competition results in computer vision, robotics, AI, or autonomous systems.

Die Zukunft der Medizin ist patientenzentriert, personalisiert und digitalisiert.

In den Alltag integrierte digitale Gesundheitslösungen sind ein unverzichtbarer Schlüssel zu einem finanziell nachhaltigen und qualitativ hochwertigen Gesundheitssystem.

title: Account Manager
description:
Mission

Gorilla is the margin intelligence platform for energy retailers. We help some of the largest energy companies in UK, Europe, the US, and Australia understand where they make and lose money, from portfolio level down to individual customer contracts.

We are entering a phase where protecting and growing our existing customer base matters as much as winning new logos. Our annual renewals represent millions in recurring revenue, and every one of them is an opportunity to deepen the relationship, expand into new modules, and prove the compounding value of our platform.

About the Role

You'll own the full commercial lifecycle of Gorilla's existing customer accounts - renewals, pricing, commercial strategy, and expansion - across a portfolio of Enterprise and Strategic accounts, primarily UK-based, with accounts also across Europe, the United States and Australia. This is a farmer role, not a hunter role: you're not chasing new logos, you're running 6–12 months ahead of every renewal, building the pricing and expansion strategy for each account, and turning retention into growth. There's no fixed playbook here.Every account sits on its own pricing history, so the role calls for real commercial creativity, not just process execution. You'll own a book of roughly £3-4m of annual renewals, measured on renewed ARR and expansion revenue from day one. Today this work sits with the CSM and the exec team on top of everything else.This hire gives our existing customers the dedicated commercial attention they deserve and frees leadership to focus on new business.

You'll own renewal negotiations, pricing and packaging, contract amendments, upsell strategy, and commercial QBR content, working closely with our Customer Success Manager, who owns product adoption and day-to-day customer engagement. When usage data shows a customer nearing capacity, you build the upgrade case. When adoption is strong, you open the expansion conversation. When there's risk, you shape the retention strategy. You turn commercial signals into growth.

Responsibilities

  • Own the full commercial renewal process across our Enterprise and Strategic accounts, maintaining a clear, accurately forecasted pipeline of timing, risk, and expected ARR.

  • Build a bespoke commercial strategy for each account — using usage data, market context, and each customer's pricing history to develop compelling business cases for additional modules and deeper integration.

  • Act on signals surfaced by the Customer Success Manager, building the expansion case commercially before renewal conversations start.

  • Map and manage multi-stakeholder accounts, from economic buyer to day-to-day champion, and know how to navigate the politics between them.

  • Lead the commercial component of QBRs and strategic reviews, translating adoption data into a value narrative and handle the harder conversations, including contract amendments, pricing corrections, and telling a customer why a price is going up.

  • Partner with our energy consultants and solution consulting team to quantify expansion value and build credible ROI narratives for customer stakeholders.

  • Feed customer and market insight back into Product and Marketing: what customers value, what they're asking for, and where the energy market is heading.

What You'll Bring

  • Real commercial creativity - the ability to build a bespoke pricing and expansion case, including quantification of the past and extrapolation of the future ROI and, from a blank page for every account, rather than executing a standard playbook. This is the single most important trait for this role.

  • Proven ownership of enterprise SaaS renewals and expansion, with six-figure+ deal sizes, measured on retained and expanded ARR; managed through relationships with 6-10 people buying committees at various layers of the customer’s organisation.

  • A strategic eye for growth levers others miss, whether that's a regulatory shift creating urgency, a new business unit that needs what we offer, or a competitor stumble that opens a door.

  • Strong negotiation instincts, equally comfortable presenting to a VP of Commercial or holding firm with a sophisticated procurement team.

  • Experience in energy, utilities, or another complex regulated vertical is a strong advantage. Our customers are energy leaders, portfolio managers and pricing leaders who expect their vendors to understand their world. If you don't come from energy, you can show you'll get there fast.

  • Familiarity with enterprise sales methodologies - we useMEDDPICC for deal scoring.

  • Structured and proactive by nature, working ahead of renewal dates rather than reacting to them.

What's in it for you

  • Flexible ways of working – We’re a hybrid-first company, with offices designed for collaboration and connection. Where there isn’t a Gorilla office nearby or regular travel to an office isn’t practical, we support remote working. From day one, you'll be equipped with the best laptop for your role, so you have everything you need to do your best work.

  • At Gorilla, we don't just watch the energy transition happen, we help make it viable. We build the intelligence layer that lets energy retailers see, steer, and protect their margins, giving them the financial clarity and operational room to invest confidently in renewables, storage, and flexibility. It's serious work with real impact on a cleaner energy system, and we have some fun along the way.

  • Core Benefits - Wherever your location, you can expect a generous PTO allowance and health insurance coverage.

  • At Gorilla, you'll work with genuinely sharp people on hard problems that matter. As we build the category leader in Energy Margin Intelligence, there's real room to leave your mark and grow your scope alongside the company. Lifelong learning is part of our DNA, and we care about your individual dreams and ambitions, beyond just work.

  • International Travel: We host Gorilla Company-Wide Gatherings where we all get a chance to see each other in real life. Past locations have included Belgium, Portugal, the Netherlands, and Spain.

You’ll own computer vision on the device, taking detection and tracking models and making them work reliably on consumer Android phones and tablets.

That means much more than getting a model to run. You’ll optimise and profile inference for real-world hardware, balancing performance with accuracy across different devices, lighting conditions and environments. You’ll work close to the camera capture pipeline, where frame timing, exposure and device behaviour can all affect the quality of the output.

Your challenge is to ensure that the data produced on a mobile device is accurate, reliable and trusted by the wider tracking system.

You’ll work closely with mobile, backend, computer vision and machine learning engineers, with the freedom to own both your technical approach and its implementation. We also embrace AI-augmented and AI-delegated development as part of how we work, enabling a small team to build and iterate at pace.

 Rattaché au responsable du Pôle vous aurez pour missions:

•    Réaliser des études de conception et piloter des études électricité dans le domaine des datacenters.

•         Elaborer des cahiers de charges techniques (Notices APS, Notices APD et CCTP) et superviser des études en phase avant-projet.

title: Cloud Engineer
description:
Wil jij impact maken bij toonaangevende enterprise klanten op het gebied van Cloud technologie?
Als Cloud engineer help je klanten hun digitale transformatie te versnellen door cloudoplossingen te ontwerpen, te realiseren en te optimaliseren. Je schakelt makkelijk tussen strategisch meedenken en operationele uitvoering, en werkt nauw samen met Itility’s Managing Consultants en Cloud engineers. Krijg je hier energie van? Dan zijn wij op zoek naar jou!


Wat jij gaat doen

Je werkt in een projectteam van bevlogen professionals aan het ontwerpen, implementeren en verbeteren van Cloud omgevingen. Samen met je collega-consultants werk je aan innovatieve projecten bij grote klanten in uiteenlopende sectoren.

Jouw werkzaamheden bestaan o.a. uit:

  • Het analyseren van klantuitdagingen en vertalen naar praktische cloudoplossingen

  • Het ontwerpen en implementeren van Cloud architecturen (bijvoorbeeld in Azure, AWS of Google Cloud)

  • Het automatiseren van infrastructuur en applicatiebeheer met behulp van IaC-tools en CI/CD-pijplijnen

  • Het verbeteren van bestaande Cloud omgevingen op het gebied van kosten, security, performance en beheerbaarheid

  • Het coachen van klanten en collega’s in het gebruik van Cloud technologie en DevOps-werkwijzen

  • Het bouwen aan een duurzame klantrelatie en het signaleren van nieuwe kansen


Bij Itility krijg je de vrijheid én ondersteuning om het beste uit jezelf te halen. Via onze eigen Itility Academy investeer je continu in je technische expertise en persoonlijke ontwikkeling. Daarnaast organiseert onze Cloud Community tech hours waarin we kennis delen, oplossingen en tools demonstreren, en samen specifieke certificaten behalen.

Daar hoort natuurlijk ook een aantrekkelijk arbeidsvoorwaardenpakket bij. Naast een salaris dat past bij jouw ervaring, achtergrond en potentie, kun je rekenen op:

  • Een Leaseauto met tankpas of een mobiliteitsvergoeding met kilometervergoeding;

  • €115 onkostenvergoeding per maand;

  • 26 vakantiedagen per jaar;

  • 50% bijdrage aan je ziektekostenverzekering van jou én die van je partner;

  • 60% bijdrage aan je pensioenregeling;

  • Een variabele bonusregeling gebaseerd op jouw persoonlijke ontwikkeling en gezamenlijke successen;

  • Laptop en telefoon;

  • Hybride werken;

  • Gebruik van gym op kantoor

Dit ben jij

Jij bent iemand die graag verantwoordelijkheid neemt, snel schakelt en altijd zoekt naar de beste oplossing. Je weet de brug te slaan tussen technologie en business, en bent in staat om complexe onderwerpen helder over te brengen. Daarnaast beschik je over:

  • Een bachelor of masterdiploma in informatica, wiskunde of elektrotechniek

  • Meer dan 3 jaar ervaring als Cloud consultant of engineer in een enterprise- of consultancy-omgeving

  • Diepgaande kennis van ten minste één Cloud platform (Azure, AWS of Google Cloud)

  • Ervaring met onderwerpen als Cloud cost control, security, networking, en monitoring

  • Vaardigheden in scripting/automation (bijv. Terraform, ARM, Bicep, Python of PowerShell)

  • Sterke communicatieve vaardigheden en een resultaatgerichte mindset

  • Een geldig Nederlands of US paspoort.

Wij bieden stageplaatsen voor meewerk- en afstudeerstages (32–40 uur per week), waarin je volop ruimte krijgt om te leren, jezelf te ontwikkelen en praktijkervaring op te doen binnen een professionele én informele werkomgeving.

Wat bieden wij jou?

  • Stagevergoeding:

    • € 300,- bruto per maand voor mbo-studenten (op basis van 40 uur per week);

    • € 400,- bruto per maand voor hbo-studenten (op basis van 40 uur per week);

  • Een leerzame stage binnen één van de modernste en duurzaamste wasserijen van Europa;

  • Kans op een (bij)baan bij Nedlin na afronding van je stage, bij wederzijdse match.

Voor welke afdelingen en opleidingen?

Techniek / Engineering / Operations
HBO: Technische Bedrijfskunde • Mechanical Engineering
MBO 3: Mechatronica • Technicus Mechatronica • Eerste monteur elektrotechnische installaties in de gebouwde omgeving • Procesoperator B

title: Werkstudent Technical Customer Support (12-24u kantoor-uren)
description:
Bij Tameson help je internationale bedrijven met vragen over industriële producten en alles wat daarbij komt kijken. Je zoekt uit welk product past bij een toepassing, vergelijkt specificaties en alternatieven, en pakt ook vragen rond bestellingen en leveringen op.
Je combineert je technisch inzicht met duidelijk klantcontact en een praktische, commerciële blik. Je bouwt snel productkennis op en leert steeds complexere vragen zelfstandig op te lossen.

Wat ga je doen?

Je draait volwaardig mee in ons team en krijgt steeds meer verantwoordelijkheid. Je:

  • analyseert technische klantvragen en zoekt passende oplossingen;

  • helpt klanten bij productselectie en technische alternatieven;

  • werkt met datasheets, specificaties en productinformatie;

  • lost vragen rond bestellingen, leveringen en retouren zelfstandig op;

  • herkent commerciële kansen en helpt klanten verder richting een aankoop;

  • stelt prioriteiten en zorgt dat klanten snel én goed worden geholpen;

  • signaleert waar onze informatie, processen of service beter kunnen.

Sommige vragen zijn eenvoudig, andere vragen echt technisch uitzoekwerk. Je hoeft onze producten nog niet te kennen, maar je moet het wel leuk vinden om te begrijpen hoe ze werken.


Wie zoeken we?

Je volgt een hbo- of wo-opleiding en bent 12-24 uur per week beschikbaar tijdens kantooruren.

Een technische studie is niet verplicht, maar een duidelijke technische achtergrond wel. Die kan bijvoorbeeld komen uit je studie, werkervaring, projecten of een technische hobby.

Daarnaast:

  • spreek en schrijf je vloeiend Nederlands, zodat je Nederlandse klanten professioneel kunt helpen;

  • begrijp je technische informatie snel en werk je graag met specificaties;

  • denk je analytisch en los je problemen graag zelf op;

  • communiceer je duidelijk en professioneel;

  • werk je nauwkeurig én efficiënt;

  • heb je commercieel gevoel;

  • neem je verantwoordelijkheid om een klantvraag echt af te ronden.

Wat bieden we?

Je krijgt een bijbaan waarin je inhoudelijk veel leert over techniek, commercie en internationale e-commerce. Naarmate je meer weet, krijg je complexere vragen en meer zelfstandigheid. Er werken meerdere studenten bij Tameson. Je studie staat voorop, dus we zijn flexibel rond colleges, veranderende roosters en tentamenperiodes. Ook kun je binnen Tameson doorgroeien. Studenten zijn bij ons tijdens hun studie al naar andere rollen doorgestroomd en sommigen zijn na hun studie fulltime bij Tameson gebleven.

Over Tameson

Tameson is een internationale e-commerceonderneming voor industriële producten. Vanuit ons kantoor op Strijp-S werken we eraan om het voor klanten zo eenvoudig mogelijk te maken om de juiste technische oplossing te vinden en te bestellen.

title: Product Manager (f/m/d)
description:
Description

We are seeking a product manager to own the "what" and "why" of our quantum sensing measurement systems. You turn customer and market needs into clear product requirements that engineering can turn into specifications, and you own the roadmap for the QDm product line, starting with QDm.1. You sit between our customers (foundries, IDMs, OSATs and failure analysis labs) and every engineering discipline, and you make sure we build the right product in the right order.


Who we are

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.


Why join us?

Picture this:

  • Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.
  • Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.
  • Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.
  • An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.
Still unsure about why joining us?
  • You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.
  • From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.
  • Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.
  • You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.
Let’s make the invisible visible!


What will you do

  • Own the product requirements: gather needs from customers, the field, the market, and internal stakeholders (serviceability, modularity and product configuration, manufacturability, and cost targets), and turn them into clear, prioritized, solution-neutral requirements.
  • Establish our requirements engineering tooling and workflow: select and set up how we capture, trace, and maintain requirements, from customer need through specification to verification, including change control across releases. This is a foundational task in your first months.
  • Own and maintain the QDm.1 roadmap: propose what gets built and in what order, make the trade-offs explicit, and align decisions with the management team.
  • Work with the applications team on customer interactions and evaluations with fabs, IDMs, OSATs and failure analysis labs, and translate what you learn into requirements.
  • For each requirement, define acceptance criteria from the customer's point of view so it is clear and testable when the need is met, and link them to customer evaluation and qualification plans.
  • Align with the Product Development department on scope and timing, and hand solution-neutral requirements into engineering: state the need and the why, and leave the how to the disciplines.
  • Support go-to-market: give input on positioning, pricing, launch readiness, and documentation scope together with the applications, operations, and product development teams.


What is expected of you

  • Several years in product management for complex hardware or capital equipment, ideally in semiconductor, metrology, or a comparable deep-tech environment.
  • A track record of writing clear product requirements that engineering can actually build from.
  • The ability to talk to both customers and engineers and to translate between them.
  • Enough technical depth to hold a credible conversation with the people designing the product, across mechanics, optics, electronics/RF, and software.
  • Structured prioritization: you make trade-offs explicit and back them with reasoning.
  • We hire for demonstrated skill rather than a specific degree; a technical or scientific background is typical. The working language is English.
Additional experience we value:
  • Semiconductor industry knowledge (fabs, IDMs, OSATs, inspection, metrology, or failure analysis).
  • Familiarity with SEMI standards and fab tool integration (for example, S2/S8, E10, SECS/GEM).
  • Experience selecting or setting up a requirements management tool (for example, Jama, Polarion, or CodeBeamer).
  • A working understanding of quantum sensing, optics, or precision instrumentation.


Our benefits

  • Mission: At QD, we’re driven by more than just building great products - we aim to make a lasting difference. Joining us means contributing to meaningful work that goes beyond business as usual.
  • Impact & growth: This is an exciting stage of our journey, and your voice matters. You’ll have the chance to shape our culture, influence key decisions, and grow alongside a company that’s scaling fast.
  • Health & fitness: With a company-sponsored Wellpass membership, you’ll have access to countless gyms, classes, and wellness offers across Germany to stay healthy and active.
  • Team & culture: We believe the best ideas come when we connect outside the office. From regular off-sites to team events, you’ll be part of a collaborative and supportive environment.
  • Well-being & balance: We value rest and recovery. That’s why you’ll enjoy 30 vacation days plus public holidays to recharge and return inspired.
  • Learning & development: Your growth is our priority. We provide an annual budget dedicated to courses, conferences, or any resources that help you expand your skills.
  • Ownership & participation: As part of our equity program, you’ll directly share in our success and the value we create together.

title: Head of Supply Chain (f/m/d) - Berlin
description:
About us

At CYCLE, we're redefining urban mobility for the people who keep cities moving: couriers, riders, and delivery pros. Our e-bike subscription service combines durable vehicles, fast repairs, and real support, everything riders need to stay on the road.
From Berlin to London, Vienna to Amsterdam, we operate in 200+ cities across Europe, providing thousands of riders with bikes built for work, not for show.
Our mission is simple: make last-mile delivery more reliable, affordable, and sustainable, one ride at a time. With every bike we deploy, we're helping build the backbone of smarter, greener cities.
Ride with us into the future - sustainable, efficient, and full speed ahead!


Your Mission

As Head of Supply Chain, you own every part of how physical goods reach our fleet and our riders, from the purchase order to the shelf to the courier's bike. You report to our Director of Operations and work directly with Hardware, Finance, Software and our country teams. In particular you will:

  • Own supply chain end to end: Purchasing, warehousing, stock keeping and outbound logistics across our European network, as one function with one owner. You ultimately ensure we have the right number of bikes, batteries and parts at the right time, the right place and the best price.
  • Oversee our assembly & refurbishment activities: Manage our assembly and refurbishment partners, own the bills of material for everything we build from purchased components as well as internal refurbishment within our locations.
  • Own the systems, not just the process: Take full responsibility for our ERP and warehouse management setup for all supply chain topics, from data model and master data through to daily execution – you will be the business owner to our software team and guide implementation.
  • Professionalize the structure: Design and implement the processes, controls and physical setup our growing operation needs, and then get your hands dirty making them real and ensuring your organization internalizes them.
  • Own the numbers behind the goods: You will guide the rest of the company on such topics as transfer prices, landed cost allocation and other supply-chain related financials, ensuring each business line's P&L is accurately reflecting parts consumption and asset usage – together with our Finance team.
  • Drive the agenda across teams: Set priorities, align Hardware, Finance and Tech behind them, and hold the line when it matters. 
  • Partner with the larger organization and understand your impact on them: All you do, you do with the end goal in mind to become the best friend of our Local and Country Operations and Sales teams, who all depend on your fulfillment excellence to grow and maintain their businesses.
  • Lead and grow your team: Build a supply chain organization that scales with us across markets.


Your skills and qualifications

We are looking for someone who has built structure inside a well-run company and is ready to build it again from scratch, with their sleeves rolled up. Ideally you bring:

  • 10+ years of relevant professional experience, of which at least 5 in a managerial supply chain or operations role.
  • Experience leading a team of at least 3 direct reports in a supply chain or operations-heavy function.
  • Structure from an established company: You have worked inside proper processes and systems and know what good looks like.
  • 0 to 1 experience: You have also built something from nothing in a smaller or fast-moving company or demonstrated you can excel in such a setting, and you are comfortable being scrappy when that is what the situation needs.
  • Commercial and financial fluency: Working capital optimization, inter-company transactions or product costing,  are all familiar territory for you.

title: Staff/Senior Software Engineer - Hydris - Golang (d/f/m)
description:
New Challenge

About Us 
Project Q GmbH ("Q") is a Germany-based DefenseTech company with offices in Berlin and Munich. We network market-available sensors, effectors, or situational awareness systems into a tactical IoT backbone that reliably provides armed forces and security agencies with cross-domain information superiority — automated, scalable, and cost-efficient.

Our solutions integrate seamlessly into existing defense and maritime infrastructures, delivering fast data fusion and AI-enhanced analytics for robust situational awareness in dynamic environments. We build platform-agnostic systems that enable real interoperability across domains.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll directly impact the technical direction of our orchestration products – Hydris – the coordination engine for sensors and mission systems, and the interoperability API that underpins it. 

You'll work at the layer where heterogeneous real-world systems like radars, AIS receivers, LoRa mesh radios, satellite feeds, and C2 platforms become a single coherent picture. The problems lie in distributed systems, protocols, and data modeling areas. They play out in environments that are bandwidth-constrained, intermittently connected, and operationally unforgiving. 

The role is deeply hands-on, but it expects you to shape what we build and how we build it, not just deliver what's specified.

What you'll do
Core engine development

  • Design and build the systems that power Hydris.
  • Go is your primary language. You should be comfortable reading Rust and TypeScript across the codebase, even if you're not writing in them day-to-day.
  • Own the architecture of a system that must run reliably on edge hardware, in disconnected mesh networks, and at scale — often all of that simultaneously.
Protocol and integration architecture
  • Evolve the schema that defines how every sensor, asset, and mission system talks to Hydris.
  • Make API design decisions that hold up across our client libraries without creating a maintenance burden.
  • Continue refining the integration framework that lets Hydris connect to new sensor types, data sources, and command systems.
  • Set the patterns for how built-in integrations (ADS-B, AIS, ASTERIX, Meshtastic, SpaceTrack, TAK, federation) are structured, tested, and maintained.
  • Make it straightforward for external developers and system vendors to build their own plugins/integrations to Hydris.
Distributed systems
  • Architect the peer-to-peer mesh and federation layer that keeps Hydris operational in disconnected, denied, intermittent, and limited-bandwidth environments.
  • Solve the hard coordination problems: conflict resolution across federated nodes, eventual consistency of entity state, and track correlation across unreliable links.
  • Ensure the system degrades gracefully rather than failing completely when connectivity is lost or constrained.
Technical leadership
  • Set technical standards for the codebase: how we test distributed behavior, how we handle protocol versioning, how we think about backward compatibility in an API-first product.
  • Review code with a focus on long-term maintainability and operational correctness, not just feature completion.
  • Make build-versus-integrate decisions and help the team clearly understand the trade-offs.

You should apply if you
  • Have built and shipped distributed systems that run in production, ideally in environments where reliability matters more than convenience.
  • Are comfortable working across the stack, from Protobuf schema design and systems-level Go, to the TypeScript that puts a map in front of a user.
  • Have well-formed views about API design and protocol evolution, informed by experience maintaining APIs that other people depend on.
  • Can operate effectively with a high degree of autonomy but are adept at collaboration with colleagues toward high-quality technical decisions, at scale.
  • Are interested in contributing to European military, maritime, and critical infrastructure defence systems.
  • Write clearly and communicate architectural decisions in a way that survives beyond the conversation where they were made. 
  • Working language is English. German is not required.
You'd be a great fit with
  • Experience with geospatial systems, sensor fusion, or track management.
  • Familiarity with defense or ISR data standards like CoT/TAK, ASTERIX, SAPIENT, MIL-STD-2525.
  • Background in networking, mesh architectures, or systems designed for contested or degraded communication environments.
  • Experience working on developer-facing open-source infrastructure where adoption depends on the quality of the API and documentation.

We Offer
  • Remote work anywhere in Germany, or hybrid/on-site in Berlin or Munich if you're already based there and prefer an office.
  • High degree of autonomy and ownership, a flat structure, and real input into technical direction.
  • Annual €1500 Learning & development budget (available after probation).
  • Bike Leasing and Urban Sports Club membership.
  • 30 days of paid time off.
Note: We're unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role – candidates must already be eligible to work in Germany.

Discovery and requirements

title: Senior Financial Controller
description:
Novar groeit hard. Het grootste zonnepark van Nederland, Eekerpolder, is inmiddels gerealiseerd en tegelijkertijd werken we aan nieuwe impactvolle projecten die bijdragen aan de energietransitie. Wat ga je doen?
Als Financial Controller ben je verantwoordelijk voor de juiste, volledige en tijdige financiële verslaglegging van meerdere Novar-entiteiten.

Je werkt nauw samen met de Head Financial Control, Financial Controllers, Project Controllers en andere collega’s binnen Finance.

 

Wat breng je mee?

Je past goed in een projectgedreven organisatie waar veel gebeurt. Je schakelt makkelijk, voelt je thuis in een omgeving waar de lijnen kort zijn en ontwikkelingen elkaar snel opvolgen. Ons aanbod

Bij Novar bieden we niet zomaar een baan, maar een uitnodiging om deel uit te maken van een betekenisvolle missie. Je werkt in een ondernemende, betrokken en innovatieve omgeving waar energie letterlijk en figuurlijk centraal staat. Samen met gedreven professionals draag je zichtbaar bij aan de verduurzaming van het energiesysteem.

Over Novar
Bij Novar, dé marktleider in de ontwikkeling van duurzame energie, dragen we elke dag ons steentje bij aan een groenere toekomst. Onze missie? Het realiseren van grootschalige turn-key projecten voor zonne-energie, energieopslag, smart grids en meer. title: Supply Chain Manager
description:
Ben jij een breed georiënteerde en daadkrachtige Supply Chain Manager die moeiteloos schakelt tussen beleid, operatie en leiderschap? Weet jij commerciële en productiebelangen perfect met elkaar te verbinden, en krijg je energie van het realiseren van hoge leverbetrouwbaarheid, optimale klanttevredenheid en efficiënte planning? Dan moeten we jou hebben!

Jouw rol

Als Supply Chain Manager ben je eindverantwoordelijk voor de volledige Supply Chain-organisatie, waaronder de productieplanning, materiaalbeheer, distributieplanning, inkoop en customer service. Samen zijn dit 7 direct reports bestaande uit 2 teamleiders en 5 operationele functies. Je ontwikkelt beleid, implementeert processen en stuurt zowel tactisch als operationeel op prestaties, efficiëntie en verbetering. Met jouw expertise en leiderschap zorg je ervoor dat onze keten soepel verloopt en toekomstbestendig blijft. Je combineert strategische visie met verbinding en hands‑on leiderschap.

Jouw werkzaamheden

  • Coachen van, en leidinggeven aan, jouw team.

  • Ontwikkelen en formuleren van de Supply Chain strategie (forecasting, planning en logistiek) en dit vertalen naar doelstellingen, budgetten en operationele acties.

  • (Mede) vormgeven van het beleid voor onze productieorganisatie als lid van het MT.

  • Verantwoordelijkheid nemen voor ingaande- en uitgaande logistieke dienstverlening door beheer van contracten, services en de daarbij horende kosten.

  • Aansturen tactisch inkoop, met als doel een stabiele aanvoer en competitieve prijzen.

  • Actief voorstellen van verbetermogelijkheden en deze implementeren voor operationeel onderhoud en het beheren van bijbehorende parameters.

  • Actieve samenwerking met interne klanten door S&OPs en benodigde afstemming op projectbasis. Forecasting volume verwachting, en vertalen lokale marktontwikkelingen naar eisen voor onze supply chain.

  • Verdiepen in ontwikkelingen in supply chains, (inter)nationale wet- en regelging, bijvoorbeeld m.b.t. CBAM, CSRD, verpakkingen en energie.

  • Binnen deze functie rapporteer je direct aan de Chief Operating Officer.

Wie ben jij?

Jij bent iemand met overzicht, besluitkracht en een duidelijke visie op Supply Chain management. Je schakelt moeiteloos tussen strategie en dagelijkse operatie en voelt je verantwoordelijk voor het volledige logistieke resultaat. Verder neem jij mee;

  • HBO+/WO richting Logistiek, Supply Chain Management of (Technische) Bedrijfskunde.

  • Ervaring voor minimaal 3 jaar binnen een leidinggevende rol in een productieomgeving zoals metaalbewerking, pharma of assemblage..

  • Sterke analytische vaardigheden en probleemoplossend vermogen.

  • Ervaring met stakeholdermanagement op meerdere niveaus.

  • Communicatief sterk en besluitvaardig.

  • Tenslotte ben je goed met digitale systemen en rapportages.

  • Je bent 36-40 uur per week beschikbaar.

Wat bieden wij jou?

Bij Heras bieden wij jou een positie binnen een zeer dynamische omgeving waarbij elke dag anders is met veel variatie en afwisseling. Je draagt je steentje bij aan een veilige omgeving en helpt om onze samenleving te beschermen creëert jouw eigen toekomst bij Heras. Daarnaast bieden wij het volgende;

  • Salaris tussen €5.000,- en €7.000,- op basis van een fulltime werkweek.

  • Een uitdagende, strategische en leidinggevende rol met veel verantwoordelijkheid.

  • Een omgeving waarin verbetering, optimalisatie en professionalisering centraal staan.

  • Laptop en telefoon voor zakelijk gebruik.

  • Reiskostenvergoeding van €0,23 per kilometer.

Heras is Europa's toonaangevende aanbieder van 360° beveiligingsoplossingen, gespecialiseerd in perimeter- en technische beveiliging om te beschermen wat belangrijk is. We ontwerpen, installeren en onderhouden complete beveiligingssystemen die naadloos aansluiten op de bedrijfsvoering van onze klanten. Zo beschermen we mensen, locaties en kritieke infrastructuur. Onze cultuur, werksfeer & waarden

Binnen Heras heerst een toegankelijke cultuur. We zijn trots op onze producten en dienstverlening en werken dagelijks volgens onze drie kernwaarden: betrokkenheid, betrouwbaarheid en deskundigheid. title: Maintenance Engineer/ Werkvoorbereider
description:
Ben jij degene die orde schept in onderhoudswerkzaamheden en ervoor zorgt dat alles op het juiste moment samenkomt? Krijg je energie van het plannen, coördineren en optimaliseren van onderhoud in een industriële omgeving? Ga met ons mee op spannende reis naar groei en het vormgeven van de toekomst van onze organisatie! We geven prioriteit aan je ontwikkeling en zorgen tegelijkertijd voor een gezonde balans tussen werk en privé.

Heidelberg Materials Nederland is momenteel op zoek naar een 

Maintenance Engineer/ Werkvoorbereider

om het team te versterken op onze cementfabriek gelegen in Rotterdam

 

Als Maintenance Engineer / Werkvoorbereider ben jij één van de belangrijke schakels in het team achter een veilige, efficiënte en betrouwbare uitvoering van onderhoudswerkzaamheden binnen onze cementfabriek. Dankzij jouw voorbereiding kunnen de monteurs en contractors hun werkzaamheden optimaal uitvoeren en blijft de beschikbaarheid van onze installaties gewaarborgd. Je vertaalt onderhoudsbehoeften naar concrete werkplannen, zorgt dat materialen, middelen en documentatie tijdig beschikbaar zijn en stemt werkzaamheden af met productie, het team en externe partijen. Daarbij houd je continu zicht op veiligheid, kwaliteit, planning en kosten. Je kijkt verder dan de dagelijkse planning alleen en denkt actief mee over verbeteringen aan onderhoudsprocessen, installaties en werkwijzen. Daarnaast speel je een belangrijke rol bij onderhoudsstops, revisies en technische projecten die bijdragen aan de betrouwbaarheid en prestaties van onze productielocatie.

Je combineert technisch inzicht met sterke organisatorische vaardigheden. Je hoeft niet de specialist te zijn, maar je begrijpt hoe een industriële installatie functioneert, weet de juiste partijen met elkaar te verbinden en zorgt ervoor dat onderhoudswerkzaamheden van voorbereiding tot uitvoering succesvol verlopen.

Wat ga jij als Maintenance Engineer/ Werkvoorbereider doen?

  • Voorbereiden, plannen en coördineren van onderhoudswerkzaamheden aan onze productie-installaties.

  • Opstellen van complete werkpakketten zodat werkzaamheden veilig, efficiënt en volgens planning kunnen worden uitgevoerd.

  • Afstemmen van onderhoudswerkzaamheden met productie, monteurs en externe contractors.

  • Ondersteunen van onderhoudsstops, revisies en technische verbeterprojecten.

  • Signaleren van verbetermogelijkheden en bijdragen aan een betrouwbare en optimale werking van onze installaties.


Wie ben jij?

Om succesvol te zijn in deze functie weet je techniek en organisatie met elkaar te verbinden. Je bent sterk in plannen en voorbereiden, houdt overzicht over meerdere werkzaamheden tegelijk en zorgt ervoor dat afspraken worden nagekomen. Daarbij schakel je gemakkelijk tussen productie, onderhoud, contractors en leveranciers.

Je voelt je thuis in een industriële omgeving en bent regelmatig op de werkvloer te vinden om werkzaamheden af te stemmen en de voortgang te bewaken. Je bent praktisch ingesteld, denkt in oplossingen en vindt het leuk om processen te verbeteren. Door jouw gestructureerde aanpak zorg je ervoor dat onderhoudswerkzaamheden veilig, efficiënt en zo goed mogelijk worden uitgevoerd.

Wat breng je mee?

 

  • HBO werk- en denkniveau, bij voorkeur in de richting Werktuigbouwkunde, Technische Bedrijfskunde, Industrial Engineering & Management of vergelijkbaar.

  • Minimaal enkele jaren ervaring binnen maintenance, werkvoorbereiding of een technische functie in een industriële omgeving.

  • Kennis van onderhoudsprocessen en ervaring met het voorbereiden, plannen en coördineren van onderhoudswerkzaamheden.

  • Een goede kennis en ervaring met SAP module PM en MM is een vereiste.

  • Een gestructureerde en proactieve werkhouding, gecombineerd met goede communicatieve vaardigheden in zowel het Nederlands als het Engels

Ons aanbod:

We bieden jou een afwisselende functie met veel zelfstandigheid binnen een klein en betrokken technisch team. Je werkt nauw samen met monteurs, productie en contractors en hebt direct invloed op de betrouwbaarheid en prestaties van onze fabriek. Binnen Heidelberg Materials krijg je volop ruimte om initiatief te nemen, jezelf verder te ontwikkelen en mee te bouwen aan een professionele onderhoudsorganisatie.

Jouw salaris ligt, afhankelijk van de ervaring die je meebrengt, tussen € 4.675 en € 6.250 bruto per maand. title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Search (remote, Europe)
description:
Hey, I'm Adrian. I’m hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join the Data Search team at Modash.

Modash helps brands find, understand, and work with creators across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. More than 2,700 companies (including Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN) use us to manage and scale their creator partnerships.

Every one of those products depends on fresh, reliable creator data. Data Core owns the systems that collect and maintain profiles for 400M+ creators across social platforms, process billions of data points, and keep the rest of Modash supplied with the raw material it needs.

That’s where you come in.

Why we're hiring

Search at Modash isn't an internal platform or a support function. It is one of the core products customers use to discover creators.

The scale is large, the data is messy, and the search intent is often complex. A customer might be looking for creators in a specific niche, people whose content conveys a certain visual style, or accounts that resemble a group they already know. Solving that well requires more than adding another filter or calling an LLM API.

We need a senior engineer who can work across the full retrieval system, from data and indexing pipelines to embeddings, ranking, relevance, and low-latency serving, and take ambiguous product problems all the way to production.

You’ll join the specialised Data Search team and work closely with Data Core, Data Insights, product teams, customers, and company leadership. You’ll have real autonomy, but you won’t work in isolation.

If you want a feel for how we think about building software, check our Engineering Blog.

What you'll actually own

1. Make creator search meaningfully better.

You’ll improve how customers discover creators across 400M+ profiles and billions of media files. That includes retrieval, filtering, ranking, relevance, speed, and the product decisions that connect them.

2. Turn multimodal data into searchable intelligence.

You’ll build systems that generate and use embeddings from images, video, text, and audio at massive scale, then make those signals useful in a real customer-facing search experience.

3. Ship new search capabilities into production.

You’ll evaluate models and technologies pragmatically, understand tradeoffs around cost, latency, and quality, and move promising approaches from experiment to a reliable production system within weeks rather than quarters.

4. Own the system end to end.

You’ll help shape the problem, gather requirements, design the architecture, write the code, release it, measure the outcome, and improve it. Senior engineers here own results, not just implementation tasks.

What the day-to-day looks like

Here’s what a typical week might include:

  • Monday. A customer search is returning technically relevant but unhelpful results. You inspect the retrieval and ranking stages, identify where intent is being lost, and propose a measurable improvement.
  • Tuesday. Deep-focus time. You build a pipeline to generate multimodal embeddings across a large batch of creator content and test how the new representation affects retrieval quality and cost.
  • Wednesday. You work with Data Insights on a new in-house datapoint. Together, you agree on its definition, coverage, and data-quality requirements, then expose it in Search to give customers more ways to discover creators.
  • Thursday. You test a reranking model on a fixed set of real customer queries. You measure how much it improves relevance against the latency and inference cost it adds, then decide what's ready for production.
  • Friday. You review production metrics, investigate a relevance regression, and share what you learned with the team. The fix may be in the model, the data, the query logic, or the product itself. You follow the evidence.

We keep meetings purposeful and protect time for deep work. You’ll have a short standup, close collaboration when it helps, and plenty of space to design, build, optimise, and launch.

Requirements

What you've done before

  • Built large-scale data or backend products. You have solid experience working with systems where volume, latency, reliability, and cost all matter.
  • Shipped products from concept to production. You’ve owned scoping, architecture, implementation, release, measurement, and iteration, not just one layer of the solution.
  • Designed distributed systems. You can reason clearly about throughput, failure modes, data flow, scalability, and operational tradeoffs.
  • Built LLM-powered or agentic features in production. You understand the practical differences between models and can balance capability against latency and cost.
  • Worked autonomously on ambiguous problems. You know how to gather requirements, ask useful questions, and turn incomplete context into forward motion.
  • Communicated clearly across teams. You can explain technical tradeoffs to engineers and non-engineers, give direct feedback, and collaborate without creating unnecessary process.
  • Worked in a fast-moving product environment. You’re comfortable learning quickly, shipping incrementally, and changing direction when the evidence does.

Bonus points if you’ve worked with multimodal embeddings, vector databases, semantic search, ranking algorithms, model deployment, self-hosted models, or GPU infrastructure. Curiosity about the creator economy helps too, but we’ll get you up to speed.

Our stack

  • AWS and GCP, with Pulumi for infrastructure as code
  • Python, TypeScript, and Node.js
  • PySpark on AWS EMR
  • Airflow
  • Milvus Vector DB through Zilliz
  • Elasticsearch
  • LLM batch APIs
  • Apache Iceberg
  • SageMaker, DynamoDB, S3, Glue, Kinesis, Lambda, ECS, and Aurora
  • Slack, GitHub, Linear, Notion, and Cursor

The interview process

We move quickly and can complete the process in under a week:

  1. Intro chat
  2. Coding interview
  3. System design interview
  4. Team interview
  5. Culture and alignment conversation with our CEO, Avery Schrader

Benefits

What we offer

  • Fully remote in Europe 🏠 Work from wherever you do your best work, with some overlap with GMT+3.

Annual salary range is 100,000€ - 130,000€ for this role. We hire across Europe, so the exact number depends on your location, employment type, skills, and experience.
  • Flexible hours ⏱ We care about outcomes, not when you log on.
  • Unlimited paid vacation 🌴 If you’re rested and happy, you do better work. Take what you need.
  • Personal development support 🧠 Courses, books, and conferences are on us when they help you grow.
  • Real ownership 💡 Take difficult search problems from idea to production without layers of unnecessary process.
  • Regular offsites ✈️ We’re remote-first, but we make time to connect, collaborate, and have fun together in person.

And a little more about us...

Founded in 2018 by a high-school dropout and a Canadian (yes, we’re also shocked it’s going so well), Modash is building a suite of tools that help brands scale partnerships with online content creators.

2,700+ companies like Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN already use Modash to manage and scale their influencer marketing work. And we're just getting started. Over the coming decade, brand investment in creators will continue to boom, and Modash will be at the centre of it all.

If you join Modash, you’ll be surrounded by people who truly want to be the greatest at their craft. People who make you better.
